target.title: fix(agents): suppress unhandled rejection from async abort callback
target.body:
## Summary

Add `.catch()` with a `process.stderr.write` diagnostic to the agent session extension abort callback. If `session.abort()` ever rejects, the rejection is logged instead of surfacing as an unhandled rejection.

This is a **defense-in-depth** hardening change. `Agent.waitForIdle()` currently resolves the active run promise, so the rejecting path is not reproducible under normal runtime conditions. The catch guards the fire-and-forget extension callback boundary so that a future regression or an extension-provided `extensionAbortHandler` override that delegates here cannot crash the process.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: `void this.abort()` in the extension callback could leave a rejected promise unhandled if `session.abort()` ever rejects.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, OpenClaw branch `fix/agent-session-void-abort-catch`

**Proof command**:
```bash
node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/proof/agent-session-abort-catch.mts
```

**Proof script output** (scripts/proof/agent-session-abort-catch.mts):
```
=== Proof: agent session extension abort catch ===

Calling extension runtime abort callback with a rejecting session.abort()...

agent-session: extension abort failed: Error: simulated abort rejection

PASS: rejecting abort is caught and logged instead of becoming an unhandled rejection.
```

The proof creates a real `AgentSession`, stubs its `abort()` to reject, invokes the bound extension runtime `abortFn`, and captures stderr to show the diagnostic is written.

**Regression test**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/agent-session.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

The regression test "logs a diagnostic when the extension abort fallback rejects" exercises the same synthetic rejecting-abort path and asserts the stderr diagnostic.

**Why stderr instead of the extension error-reporting path**: the abort callback is fire-and-forget (`void ...`) and runs when the extension runtime may already be tearing down. `process.stderr.write` is the lowest-level, synchronous sink available and matches other emergency diagnostics in the session boundary. The extension error listener is not used because the callback must not itself throw or await async reporting.

## Risk

Low. Error logged to stderr for observability; no change to happy-path behavior.

target.title: feat(chat-ui): syntax-highlighted code blocks and native tables in chat markdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Assistant messages in the shared chat UI rendered fenced code without syntax highlighting and GFM tables as raw pipe characters, because the whole message went through a single `AttributedString(markdown:)` → `Text` pass that supports neither.

Part of #100195

## Why This Change Was Made

Instead of swapping in a heavy markdown UI dependency, the message is now segmented before rendering (`ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenter`): prose keeps the existing AttributedString pipeline, completed fenced code renders through a lightweight per-language tokenizer (keywords/strings/comments/numbers for swift, kotlin, typescript/javascript, python, bash, json — unknown languages pass through unstyled), and valid GFM tables (header + delimiter row, alignment-aware, escaped-pipe handling) render as a native SwiftUI `Grid`. Anything ambiguous falls back to prose unchanged. The streaming path stays cheap: a fence or table still open at the stream tail renders as plain text, and completed blocks are memoized in a bounded content-keyed highlight cache so deltas never re-tokenize finished work. No new dependency was added: the evaluated highlighting package is dormant upstream and only covers Swift grammar. The old fence/table tracking inside the soft-break preprocessor became dead and was deleted.

## User Impact

Assistant replies show syntax-highlighted code blocks (branded mono typography, language label, horizontal scrolling, light/dark-adaptive colors) and real tables instead of raw `|` runs, on both platforms consuming the shared chat UI (iOS and macOS). Streaming responsiveness is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`: `swift build` green; `swift test --filter "ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenterTests|ChatCodeHighlighterTests|ChatMarkdownDisplayPreprocessorTests"` → 43/43 pass (fence info strings, nested ```/~~~, indent dedent, 4-space non-fence, unclosed-fence streaming fallback, trailing-table streaming fallback, alignments, escaped pipes, row pad/truncate, count-mismatch prose fallback).
- `apps/macos`: `swift build` green (shared package consumer).
- Highlight smoke tests assert token classification and byte-exact source preservation.
- Codex autoreview on the commit: one P1 finding, rejected as a false positive — it claimed `Double` components can't be passed to `CGFloat` color initializers, but SE-0307 implicit conversion applies and both platform builds compile the file as-is.

Known gap: rendering verified by compile + unit tests; no simulator screenshot pass yet (dark/light palettes use the same dynamic-provider pattern as `OpenClawChatTheme`).

target.title: feat(android): read-only offline cache for chat sessions and transcripts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold-opening the chat tab shows a blank screen until the gateway responds, and when the gateway is unreachable there is nothing to read at all. Previously fetched conversations were held only in memory and lost on every process restart.

Part of #100194

## Why This Change Was Made

The app already has everything needed for a read-only cache: a stable per-gateway endpoint identity (the same id used for TLS fingerprint pinning) and a history reconciliation path that drops stale responses via generation tracking. This change adds a small, disposable Room database (androidx.room via KSP) that write-throughs live `chat.history` / `sessions.list` results and replays them on the next cold open. No merge algorithm was invented: cached rows are emitted first, then the live response replaces them wholesale through the existing reconciliation path, which also keeps list item identity stable. The cache is bounded (50 sessions, 200 newest messages per session, eviction on write), schema-versioned with destructive migration only, and stores text parts only — attachments and binary content never reach disk. Cache rows are keyed by the gateway's stable identity so transcripts cannot cross gateways; pairing/auth resets purge the database, and gateway-side session deletes purge the matching cached rows.

## User Impact

- Chat opens instantly with the last-known transcript, then updates in place when live history arrives.
- While the gateway is unreachable, the session list and cached transcripts remain browsable read-only; sending is still blocked by the existing health gate.
- The cache is disposable: any schema change drops and rebuilds it; no user action or migration ever required.
- Licenses screen: no new notice file needed — the bundled license list convention excludes androidx artifacts.
- Possible follow-up if reviewers want it: encryption-at-rest for the cache DB (it currently relies on app-private storage, like other app databases).

## Evidence

- `cd apps/android && ./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.*'` — green (59 tests, 13 new); full `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` suite green (run twice, incl. after final changes).
- New tests: `RoomChatTranscriptCacheTest` (round-trip, text-only rows, 200/50 bounds + eviction incl. full-cache deep-session case, gateway-identity scoping, delete/clear purges) and `ChatControllerTranscriptCacheTest` (offline cold open shows cache + send stays blocked, cache-first emission then wholesale live replacement with stable message ids and write-through, offline session switch, delete-event purge).
- Codex autoreview: 4 cycles; two accepted findings fixed with regression tests (full-cache eviction edge, session-delete purge); final run clean.

Known gaps: sub-coroutine-step cross-gateway write race during an active gateway switch (self-heals on next write; strict fix needs connection-epoch plumbing — follow-up); per-message events deliberately not written through (cache refreshes on each online open); no on-device instrumentation pass.

target.title: fix: prevent Anthropic thinking-signature replay causing permanent session bricks (#94228)
target.body:
## Summary

This PR implements a create-side prevention fix for Issue #94228, where Anthropic thinking-signature replay causes permanent session bricks.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: The current implementation re-emits ALL historical thinking blocks with their original signatures during replay, violating Anthropic's contract that "thinking blocks from already-closed turns may be omitted". When signatures become stale (due to model version drift, config changes, or internal state corruption), this causes HTTP 400 errors and permanent session bricks (~11 occurrences/24h per host).

**Impact**: Users experience permanent session bricks requiring manual restart when thinking signatures no longer match the replay context.

## Why This Change Was Made

After analyzing 9 different PR approaches (#94493, #94649, #97019, etc.), I identified a gap in the existing sanitization pipeline:

- Current code handles compaction-stale signatures (timestamp-based)
- Current code handles blank/missing signatures
- **Missing**: Present-but-invalid signatures from other sources (model drift, config changes, corruption)

This fix fills that gap by unconditionally stripping ALL non-latest thinking signatures, providing defense-in-depth alongside recovery-side approaches like PR #94649.

## User Impact

**Before**: Sessions could brick permanently when stale thinking signatures were replayed, causing HTTP 400 errors on every subsequent request.

**After**: Non-latest thinking signatures are proactively stripped before replay, preventing signature mismatch errors while preserving latest-turn signatures for provider compatibility.

**Performance**: Minimal impact - returns original array reference when no changes needed (reference equality optimization).

## Evidence

### Code Changes
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/thinking.ts`: Added `stripAllNonLatestThinkingSignatures()` (+62 lines)
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts`: Integrated into `sanitizeSessionHistory` pipeline (+16 lines)
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/thinking.test.ts`: Comprehensive test coverage (+152 lines)

### Test Coverage
6 test cases covering:
1. Reference equality when no non-latest turns exist
2. Strips ALL signature types (valid, blank, missing, opaque) from non-latest turns
3. Preserves all signatures with single turn + preserveLatestAssistant: false
4. Can strip from "latest" turn when flag disabled
5. Handles multiple turns correctly
6. Generates placeholder text for thinking-only turns

### Design Principles
- **Minimal scope**: ~60 lines core logic, following PR #94649 example
- **Leverages existing helpers**: Uses `stripThinkingSignaturesFromMessage`
- **Defensive design**: Latest-turn exemption protects provider expectations
- **Performance optimized**: Returns original array when unchanged
- **Comprehensive testing**: 6 cases covering edge cases

### Integration Point
Inserted into `sanitizeSessionHistory` pipeline between:
1. `stripStaleThinkingSignaturesForCompactionReplay` (compaction-specific)
2. **NEW** `stripAllNonLatestThinkingSignatures` (universal prevention)
3. `stripInvalidThinkingSignatures` (final safety net)

## Relationship to Other Fixes

This create-side prevention complements PR #94649 recovery-side approach:

| Layer | Mechanism | Timing | This PR | PR #94649 |
|-------|-----------|--------|---------|-----------|
| Prevention | Create-side sanitization | Before request sent | ✅ Strips non-latest signatures | ❌ |
| Recovery | Terminal-result carrier | After error detected | ❌ | ✅ Retries without thinking |
| Repair | Reactive history repair | After provider confirms rejection | ❌ | ✅ `repairRejectedThinkingReplayInSessionManager` |

Three layers working together provide robust protection against thinking-signature bricks.

## Testing Notes

Due to network firewall blocking external AI APIs (`api.anthropic.com` redirected to block page), I could not perform live reproduction of the thinking-signature brick scenario. Implementation based on thorough source code analysis across 9 different PR approaches.

Tests can be validated via CI or by maintainers with direct API access.

## Coordination Questions

- Is this PR waiting on any other PR to merge first?
- Are maintainers planning coordinated fix under #94228, or preferring incremental patches?
- Should contributors focus on one approach (recovery vs prevention) to avoid conflicts?

Happy to help however makes sense - whether providing additional repro evidence (once network access resolved), testing existing PRs, or diving into narrower follow-up issues!

target.title: feat(ios): read-only offline cache for chat sessions and transcripts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where opening the chat tab showed a blank transcript until the gateway responded, and showed nothing at all when the gateway was unreachable. All chat state was in memory only, so cold opens and offline periods left users staring at an empty screen even for conversations they had just been reading.

Part of #100194

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a small, disposable, read-only offline cache of recent chat sessions and transcripts, scoped per paired gateway identity. Cold opens paint the last known transcript immediately and the live gateway history then replaces it wholesale through the existing reconciliation path; the gateway remains the single source of truth whenever connected. The store is versioned SQLite with drop-and-rebuild on any mismatch — no migrations, no dual source of truth, no new dependencies. Text rows only; attachment payloads are never persisted, and the database uses complete-until-first-unlock file protection. The seam lives in the shared chat package behind a protocol (`OpenClawChatTranscriptCache`), so the macOS app can adopt it later; its call sites are untouched.

## User Impact

The chat tab now renders the last known conversation instantly on launch instead of a blank screen, and the session list plus recent transcripts stay browsable while disconnected. Sending stays disabled until the connection is healthy, exactly as before. Transcripts are cached per paired gateway and can never appear under a different gateway.

## Evidence

- `cd apps/shared/OpenClawKit && swift test --filter "ChatTranscriptCacheStoreTests|ChatViewModelTranscriptCacheTests"` — 15/15 pass: store round-trip, bounds (50 sessions / 50 transcripts / 200 messages), eviction order, gateway-identity scoping, schema/corruption drop-and-rebuild, attachment stripping; view-model tests prove cache-first paint then wholesale live replace, offline browsing after a failed history request, write-through of live history, and that live responses (including empty ones) always win over slow cache reads.
- `pnpm ios:build` (xcodebuild, iPhone 17 simulator, including SwiftFormat/SwiftLint phases) — BUILD SUCCEEDED.
- Existing `ChatViewModelTests` suite (105 tests) passes; no behavior change when no cache is injected (the parameter defaults to nil).
- Codex autoreview: 3 rounds; two accepted findings fixed with regression tests (stale cached sessions vs. live empty list; view-model recreation on paired-gateway switch so cache scopes can never cross), final round clean ("patch is correct", 0.82).

Known gaps: no on-device airplane-mode pass (view-model-level proof via scripted transport); cache rows for a forgotten gateway linger until evicted — hooking gateway "forget" to a purge is a follow-up. Note: `TalkConfigContractTests.selectionFixtures` and parallel-load `ChatViewModelTests` flakes reproduce on clean `origin/main` (verified with this diff stashed) — pre-existing, tracked separately.

target.title: fix(imessage): false group drop-all startup warning when groupAllowFrom is set without groups
target.body:
Related: #78749

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running iMessage with `groupPolicy: "allowlist"` plus a sender allowlist (`channels.imessage.groupAllowFrom`, or the `allowFrom` fallback) but no `channels.imessage.groups` map would see a false startup warning claiming `Every inbound group message will be dropped` — even though group messages flow fine in that configuration via sender-level filtering (`senderFilterBypass` in `src/config/group-policy.ts`).

The warning's remedy text was also wrong for the real drop-all case: it recommended adding `groups["*"]`, but with an empty effective `groupAllowFrom` the sender gate (`group_policy_empty_allowlist`) blocks every group message regardless of `groups` content, so following the advice would not stop the drops.

## Why This Change Was Made

The startup warning now mirrors the runtime gate exactly: `warnGroupAllowlistMisconfigOnce` takes `hasGroupAllowFrom`, computed with the same shared helper (`mergeIMessageGroupAllowFromWithLegacyChatTargets`, now exported) and the same inputs the per-message gate receives, and fires only when both the `groups` registry and the effective group sender allowlist are empty — the only configuration where drop-all is provable at startup (route-level sender allowlists can admit senders later, so any broader condition would reintroduce false positives). The warning text now names `groupAllowFrom` as the actual fix. The stale file-header comment and the two-gate docs section were updated to describe the two warnings' distinct triggers and remedies.

## User Impact

Operators using `groupPolicy: "allowlist"` with `groupAllowFrom` (or the `allowFrom` fallback) and no `groups` map no longer get a misleading warn-level log at every gateway start. Operators in the genuine drop-all configuration now get remediation guidance that actually unblocks group messages.

## Evidence

- False positive confirmed against current gating behavior: `resolveChannelGroupPolicy` admits groups via `senderFilterBypass` (`src/config/group-policy.ts:408`), covered by `extensions/imessage/src/monitor.gating.test.ts` dispatch tests with `groupAllowFrom` set and no `groups`.
- New unit test proves the warning stays silent when `hasGroupAllowFrom` is true, and existing warning tests updated for the new condition/message: `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/group-allowlist-warnings.test.ts` (12 pass).
- Focused suites pass locally via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`: gating + inbound-processing (52 pass), monitor startup paths `monitor.watch-subscribe-retry` / `monitor-provider.echo-cache` / `channel.runtime` (22 pass).
- Remote `check:changed` lane green on Blacksmith Testbox (extensions typecheck, extension-test typecheck, changed-file lint 0 warnings/0 errors, guards), plus `oxfmt --check` clean on the touched files.
- Codex autoreview: one accepted docs finding (first docs draft implied both warnings fire for the same config) fixed; rerun clean — "no accepted/actionable findings".

target.title: feat(control-ui): session grouping with drag & drop and channel categorization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI sessions table is a flat list. Once an operator runs many sessions across agents and message channels (Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, ...), there is no way to organize them: no grouping, no way to categorize channel-originated sessions, and no equivalent of the desktop app's custom session groups.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a persistent per-session `category` field end-to-end (gateway protocol `sessions.patch` -> session store -> list rows -> live session-change events) and a "Group by" control on the web Sessions page with None / Custom groups / Channel / Kind / Agent / Date modes. The field is named `category` to stay clearly separate from the existing chat-group concepts (`groupId`, `groupChannel`, kind `group`). Custom group membership persists server-side on the session entry; empty just-created groups live in browser localStorage until a session is assigned. Cleared categories emit an explicit `null` in session events so other connected clients drop the group during merge-reconcile instead of going stale.

## User Impact

- Group the sessions table by custom groups, channel, kind, agent, or date, with section headers and counts; the chosen mode persists per browser.
- Create custom groups and assign sessions by dragging rows onto a section (drop-target highlight), or via a per-row group selector; sessions from message channels can be categorized like any other session.
- Channel mode buckets sessions by their originating channel out of the box.
- Group names are searchable in the table filter and shown in the session details panel.
- Protocol change is additive: `sessions.patch` accepts `category: string | null`; session rows and change events carry `category`.

## Evidence

- Backend: `sessions-patch` suite 239 passed (new category persist/trim/clear/duplicate/empty tests), `server.sessions.list-changed` 46 passed after the event payload change, protocol + session-utils + store-rpc 690 passed.
- UI: 42 tests passed, including new coverage for grouping helpers (channel/agent/date/category bucketing, group ordering), section headers and counts, drag-drop assignment via header drop targets, the filtered empty state under active grouping, and reconcile dropping a cleared category.
- `tsgo` core and UI lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files.
- Codex autoreview (gpt-5.5) over four rounds; the three accepted findings (blank empty state when grouped, `agent:main:main` misgrouped in Agent mode, stale category on other clients after clear) were fixed with regression tests; final run reported no actionable findings.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui.md` describes the new grouping behavior.

target.title: fix(acp): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in printSessionUpdate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `printSessionUpdate` helper in `src/acp/client.ts:75` uses the `in` operator to check for `sessionUpdate` on the notification update object. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so it would match inherited properties — though unlikely in practice, `Object.hasOwn()` is the more correct semantic for own-property checks.

## Changes

- **`src/acp/client.ts`** — replace `!("sessionUpdate" in update)` with `!Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate")` (1 line)

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — Object.hasOwn on ACP session notification data

The proof script mirrors the exact `printSessionUpdate` logic and exercises it against realistic ACP `SessionNotification` objects matching the `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` schema (where `sessionUpdate` is a required discriminator const on every `SessionUpdate` union arm).

```text
$ node scripts/proof-99363-printSessionUpdate.mjs
==============================================================
Proof: PR #99363 — Object.hasOwn in printSessionUpdate
==============================================================

📋 Test 1: All ACP sessionUpdate discriminator variants
--------------------------------------------------
  [agentMessageChunk] → matched=true, action="write text to stdout"
  ✅ PASS: agentMessageChunk: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [toolCall] → matched=true, action="log tool read_file (in_progress)"
  ✅ PASS: toolCall: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [toolCallUpdate] → matched=true, action="log update tool_001: completed"
  ✅ PASS: toolCallUpdate: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [availableCommandsUpdate] → matched=true, action="log commands: /help /status"
  ✅ PASS: availableCommandsUpdate: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [nonSessionUpdate] → matched=false, action="undefined"
  ✅ PASS: nonSessionUpdate: should NOT match (no sessionUpdate)

📋 Test 2: Object.hasOwn vs `in` operator — own-property equivalence
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): true
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               true
  ✅ PASS: Both return true for own property

📋 Test 3: Prototype pollution safety — Object.hasOwn advantage
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.prototype.sessionUpdate injected → "agent_message_chunk"
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): false ← correctly rejects injected
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               true ← incorrectly matches injected
  ✅ PASS: Object.hasOwn correctly REJECTS prototype-injected property
  ✅ PASS: in operator INCORRECTLY matches prototype-injected property
  ✅ PASS: Object.prototype.sessionUpdate removed after cleanup

📋 Test 4: Missing property — both operators agree
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): false
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               false
  ✅ PASS: Both return false for missing property

==============================================================
Results: 10 passed, 0 failed out of 10 assertions
==============================================================

✅ PROOF PASSED — Object.hasOwn behavior is correct for ACP session updates.

Key findings:
  1. Object.hasOwn and `in` operator behave identically for normal ACP
     session update discriminator properties (all 4 update types pass).
  2. Object.hasOwn correctly rejects non-session-update notifications
     that lack a sessionUpdate own property.
  3. Object.hasOwn provides prototype pollution safety: unlike `in`,
     it does NOT match a prototype-injected sessionUpdate property.
  4. The ACP SDK schema requires sessionUpdate as a required discriminator
     on every SessionUpdate union arm — so in practice both are equivalent,
     but Object.hasOwn is the more defensive, semantically correct choice.
```

N/A (self-contained code hygiene improvement)

## Changes

|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.core.ts` | Accept `models.providers.*.baseURL`, normalize it to canonical `baseUrl`, delete the alias before downstream code reads the provider config, and reject configs that set both spellings. |
| `src/config/schema.hints.ts` | Walk Zod pipes while collecting schema hint paths so transformed provider schemas keep sensitive URL metadata for `models.providers.*.baseUrl` and its `baseURL` alias. |
| `src/config/schema.test.ts` | Covers `baseURL` normalization, alias deletion, duplicate-spelling rejection, and sensitive URL metadata on the alias path. |

| `packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts` | Covers the alias in the shared sensitive URL path predicate. |
| `src/agents/memory-search.ts` | Keeps the direct built-in memory adapter when one exists. The OpenAI memory adapter already reads canonical provider `baseUrl`, so routing should stay on the existing adapter instead of becoming an unconfigured provider. |

## What Problem This Solves

TUI `/new` switched to an empty local key without running the existing Gateway session-creation lifecycle. Command hooks, `before_reset`, `session_end`, and `session_start` therefore missed TUI new-session transitions, so features such as session-memory hooks could not capture the completed parent conversation. ## Why This Change Was Made

- Route both Gateway and embedded TUI backends through that service; no new protocol field or TUI-specific core policy.

target.title: fix(gateway): preserve abort after dispatch rejection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #90999.

Users can see contradictory or missing terminal state when `chat.send` dispatch fails around abort/session-lifecycle timing. The bad windows are:

- abort already won, but a later post-dispatch rejection can overwrite the cached terminal result as an error;
- dispatch already failed, but a late `chat.abort` during fallback persistence can mask the real error as an abort;
- a queued followup was accepted, then an explicit abort won before dispatch rejection, and the accepted-followup branch could otherwise bypass the abort-preserve dedupe write;
- session lifecycle interruption after `chat.send` ACK can abort the controller without going through the normal `chat.abort` marker/broadcast path, leaving the client without a terminal `chat` event or keeping the session admission busy after terminal abort.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict refresh keeps current `main` session-admission, queued-followup, and dispatch-error lifecycle behavior, then makes terminal ownership explicit:

- if `chat.abort` already recorded the abort marker, preserve the abort terminal result, write the aborted dedupe, release session admission/active-run ownership before fallback persistence, and do not resurrect the run as an error;
- if a followup was already queued and no explicit abort marker owns the run, keep that accepted client run terminal;
- if dispatch/error owns the terminal state, close abortability before any awaited fallback persistence, clear stale abort state, cache the error, and broadcast the error;
- if lifecycle admission interrupts the run, do not treat a bare aborted signal as proof that a terminal abort was already broadcast.

The PR remains limited to `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` and `src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts`.

## User Impact

`chat.send` clients now receive one stable terminal outcome for these race windows. Same-run retries observe the correct cached terminal result, late abort does not rewrite a real dispatch error, lifecycle-interrupted sends still produce a terminal `chat` event, queued followup admission still terminalizes the accepted client run unless an explicit abort owns the run, and lifecycle operations are not held behind unrelated fallback transcript persistence after a terminal abort.

Related: #84176 and #84306.

target.title: fix(core): use UTF-16-safe truncation for chat display, ACP stream relay, and native hook relay
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three truncation helpers in core used raw `String.prototype.slice`, which can split supplementary-plane characters (emoji, CJK extension B+, etc.) into lone surrogate halves when the cutoff lands between a high/low surrogate pair. This produces malformed UTF-16 in user-visible display text — the same class of bug as #99566, which fixed the exec approval command display path.

| Site | Cap | Risk |
|------|-----|------|
| `chat-display-projection.ts` — `truncateChatHistoryText` | 8 KiB | Very high — core display pipeline, every chat message goes through it, messages frequently contain emoji |
| `acp-spawn-parent-stream.ts` — `truncate()` | 220 chars | High — short boundary, agent streaming output often contains emoji; collision probability much higher than #99566's 16 KiB cap |
| `native-hook-relay.ts` — `truncateText()` | 80/240/700 chars | Medium-high — approval UI (title, description, command key), same exec-approval-command-display security decision surface as #99566 |

## Summary

- Switch all three truncation helpers to the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` from `src/shared/utf16-slice.js` (the same helper introduced in #99566).
- Add regression tests: construct a string with an emoji whose surrogate pair crosses the truncation boundary, verify no lone surrogate in output.
- The fix is mechanical: each site changes one `value.slice(0, N)` call to `truncateUtf16Safe(value, N)` and adds one import.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts` — 4 files, 12 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/acp-spawn-parent-stream.test.ts` — 1 file, 35 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts` — 1 file, 77 tests passed
- `pnpm exec oxlint` on all 6 changed files — 0 warnings
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1` on all 6 changed files — clean
- Confirmed via runtime: the acp-spawn-parent-stream test places `😀` at positions 218-219 so old `slice(0, 219)` produces a lone high surrogate (0xD83D); `truncateUtf16Safe` correctly backs off to 218

## Risk

Low. This only changes the truncation boundary to back off from split surrogate pairs. It does not change truncation caps, markers, redaction logic, or any product behavior. The shared helper is dependency-free (no `node:` imports) and already used in production in `exec-approval-command-display.ts` since #99566 landed.

target.title: fix(macos): prevent hatch and web chat from timing out on slow first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS onboarding/web chat could make a slow first assistant reply look stuck or prematurely timed out when the selected model takes longer than the old client-side budget. This matters for first-run hatch/chat paths with slower models such as OpenAI 5.5, where the user expects the assistant to keep working after they describe its purpose.

The mismatch was that the macOS WebChat path needed a longer assistant-run budget and a completion observation path, while the request/ACK deadline should still fail quickly when the gateway is unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates the short request/ACK deadline from the actual WebChat assistant run budget. The shared `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default stays request-sized so other macOS callers such as Talk Mode keep their existing timeout policy, while `MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage` explicitly opts WebChat/hatch into a five-minute `timeoutMs` run budget.

The shared chat UI now reads its pending/completion budget from the transport: default transports keep the existing 120-second pending wait, and macOS WebChat explicitly opts into the five-minute window through `MacGatewayChatTransport.pendingRunTimeoutMs`. macOS WebChat also waits for completion through existing Gateway `agent.wait` before refreshing history. The change uses existing Gateway surfaces (`chat.send.timeoutMs` and `agent.wait`) and does not change gateway protocol shape, auth, provider routing, model selection, session storage, schema, migrations, iOS transport behavior, or delivery channels.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant now get a realistic wait window and a production completion observation path for slow first replies instead of a premature timeout or stuck-looking state while the assistant run may still be active or recently completed.

The intended behavior is that macOS WebChat/hatch keeps gateway ACK failures prompt while giving only the WebChat assistant run, UI pending state, and completion refresh path the first-run-sized five-minute window. Shared/default chat transports keep the existing 120-second pending budget unless they explicitly opt into a longer one.

## Evidence

Native macOS visual/accessibility proof on the PR build, using the native `OpenClaw Chat` window and a session-level `openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` override for this proof run:

```text

prompt=For local PR #97722 native WebChat visual proof only: use the shell tool to run exactly `sleep 45` with no output, then reply exactly `native WebChat slow reply proof complete`.
```

At +32 seconds, the native macOS window was still connected and still showed the assistant pending state instead of a 30-second timeout/error:

target.title: fix(acp): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in printSessionUpdate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `printSessionUpdate` helper in `src/acp/client.ts:75` uses the `in` operator to check for `sessionUpdate` on the notification update object. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so it would match inherited properties — though unlikely in practice, `Object.hasOwn()` is the more correct semantic for own-property checks.

## Changes

- **`src/acp/client.ts`** — replace `!("sessionUpdate" in update)` with `!Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate")` (1 line)

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — Object.hasOwn on ACP session notification data

The proof script mirrors the exact `printSessionUpdate` logic and exercises it against realistic ACP `SessionNotification` objects matching the `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` schema (where `sessionUpdate` is a required discriminator const on every `SessionUpdate` union arm).

```text
$ node scripts/proof-99363-printSessionUpdate.mjs
==============================================================
Proof: PR #99363 — Object.hasOwn in printSessionUpdate
==============================================================

📋 Test 1: All ACP sessionUpdate discriminator variants
--------------------------------------------------
  [agentMessageChunk] → matched=true, action="write text to stdout"
  ✅ PASS: agentMessageChunk: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [toolCall] → matched=true, action="log tool read_file (in_progress)"
  ✅ PASS: toolCall: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [toolCallUpdate] → matched=true, action="log update tool_001: completed"
  ✅ PASS: toolCallUpdate: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [availableCommandsUpdate] → matched=true, action="log commands: /help /status"
  ✅ PASS: availableCommandsUpdate: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [nonSessionUpdate] → matched=false, action="undefined"
  ✅ PASS: nonSessionUpdate: should NOT match (no sessionUpdate)

📋 Test 2: Object.hasOwn vs `in` operator — own-property equivalence
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): true
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               true
  ✅ PASS: Both return true for own property

📋 Test 3: Prototype pollution safety — Object.hasOwn advantage
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.prototype.sessionUpdate injected → "agent_message_chunk"
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): false ← correctly rejects injected
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               true ← incorrectly matches injected
  ✅ PASS: Object.hasOwn correctly REJECTS prototype-injected property
  ✅ PASS: in operator INCORRECTLY matches prototype-injected property
  ✅ PASS: Object.prototype.sessionUpdate removed after cleanup

📋 Test 4: Missing property — both operators agree
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): false
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               false
  ✅ PASS: Both return false for missing property

==============================================================
Results: 10 passed, 0 failed out of 10 assertions
==============================================================

✅ PROOF PASSED — Object.hasOwn behavior is correct for ACP session updates.

Key findings:
  1. Object.hasOwn and `in` operator behave identically for normal ACP
     session update discriminator properties (all 4 update types pass).
  2. Object.hasOwn correctly rejects non-session-update notifications
     that lack a sessionUpdate own property.
  3. Object.hasOwn provides prototype pollution safety: unlike `in`,
     it does NOT match a prototype-injected sessionUpdate property.
  4. The ACP SDK schema requires sessionUpdate as a required discriminator
     on every SessionUpdate union arm — so in practice both are equivalent,
     but Object.hasOwn is the more defensive, semantically correct choice.
```

target.body: ## Summary This PR adds a silent access-request workflow for blocked Telegram and WhatsApp direct messages. - Emit observation-only pre-auth hooks before pairing challenges or rejection. - Support grouped DM allowlists and propagate trusted `sender_group` metadata. - Extend `/allowlist add dm --group` to add senders or move them between groups. - Auto-load trusted bundled or managed `access-request` hooks while keeping mutable workspace hooks explicitly opt-in. - Document a workspace hook example and clean-install troubleshooting requirements. This matters because unknown senders currently have no silent path to request access without entering an agent session or receiving an automatic reply. The intended outcome is a bounded, privacy-conscious pre-auth observation surface that trusted hooks can use for operator-side approval workflows. Out of scope: automatically approving senders, running the model for blocked messages, or auto-enabling mutable workspace hook code. Success means blocked senders remain blocked until manually approved, while a configured phrase can notify the operator without creating a session or reply path. Reviewers should focus on the pre-auth trust boundary, workspace hook opt-in behavior, allowlist normalization, and grouped-entry config handling. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? N/A - no linked issue. Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? N/A. Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No known maintainer or owner request. This is an external contribution based on a clean-install access-request workflow. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Unknown Telegram and WhatsApp DM senders can silently request manual access without creating an agent session, running the model, or receiving a reply. - Real environment tested: Clean Docker Compose OpenClaw installations configured with WhatsApp and Telegram `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and an explicitly enabled workspace `access-request` hook. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Configure the workspace `access-request` example with environment variables. 2. Run `openclaw config set tools.profile messaging`. 3. Run `openclaw config set commands.config true`. 4. Recreate the container with `docker compose down && docker compose up -d`. 5. Send the configured access phrase from a blocked WhatsApp number. 6. Approve the sender from the operator chat with `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp --group restricted `. - Evidence after fix: 1. WhatsApp blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 2. Operator receives the silent WhatsApp access request notification. 3. WhatsApp sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp`. 4. WhatsApp admitted sender receives a normal agent response. 5. Telegram blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 6. Operator receives the silent Telegram access request notification. 7. Telegram sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel telegram`. - Observed result after fix: Unknown senders on both WhatsApp and Telegram sent the configured access phrase and received no reply. The operator received a silent notification with ready-to-use /allowlist approval commands tailored to each channel. After approval, the sender was admitted to the restricted group. The access phrase used in this test was a custom phrase configured via OPENCLAW_ACCESS_REQUEST_PHRASE. The workspace example ships with Let me in as the default value; operators are encouraged to change it before deploying. - What was not tested: Multi-account deployments were not tested live. - Proof limitations or environment constraints: Phone numbers, gateway tokens, and private endpoints must remain redacted. - Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this PR, blocked senders were rejected before any trusted pre-auth observation hook existed. ## Tests and validation Commands run: ```bash node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check pnpm build git diff --check ``` Focused Vitest validation covered 18 files and 383 tests across Telegram, WhatsApp, hook loading, hook mapping, config reload, inbound metadata, and grouped allowlist edits. Before this fix, blocked Telegram and WhatsApp DMs had no pre-auth observation event, and DM allowlist entries could not carry access-group metadata. ## Risk checklist Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. The config schema adds optional grouped DM `allowFrom` entries. Existing string entries remain supported. target.title: fix(openai): bound Codex image generation no-body response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM gap in OpenAI Codex OAuth image generation. The Codex Responses SSE path already bounds streamed bodies in `readResponseBodyText`, but the `!response.body` branch still called `response.text()` and only checked `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` after buffering the full payload. A faulty or hostile endpoint returning a body without a readable stream could still grow gateway memory without bound before the size guard fired.

## Why This Change Was Made

The no-body branch now fail-closes before any full-buffer fallback:

- reject oversized bodies from a trustworthy `Content-Length` header before calling `readResponseWithLimit` / `arrayBuffer()`
- reject missing or invalid `Content-Length` when no readable stream exists, instead of reading an unknown-size body
- only read bounded no-body payloads when `Content-Length` is present and within `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` (64 MiB)

This follows the same invariant as the existing streamed Codex image SSE guard:

- streamed Codex image SSE responses remain incrementally capped and cancelled on overflow
- no-body Codex image responses now reject early from `Content-Length` or fail closed when length is unknown
- loopback transport proof exercises the production Codex OAuth image path over real HTTP on `127.0.0.1`

## User Impact

Operators using Codex OAuth image generation through the Responses transport are protected when a provider returns an oversized or unknown-size payload on the no-body response path. Valid Codex image SSE responses continue to work unchanged.

## Evidence

Loopback transport proof: I ran the production Codex OAuth `generateImage` path against a local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`. This uses the real `postJsonRequest` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` path, real HTTP `Response` streams/headers, OAuth auth stubbing only, and no mocked `postJsonRequest`.

target.title: fix(gateway): redact Responses media blocks in chat history sanitization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing chat history in Control UI / WebChat would still receive embedded `data:` image payloads on Responses-style media blocks (`input_image.image_url` and legacy `image.url`) after history sanitization, even though other base64 and data-URL media paths were already redacted.

Also fixes CI failures in `chat.directive-tags.test.ts`: live WebChat broadcast must keep `{ type: "input_image", image_url: "data:..." }` for QR/image delivery, so inline media redaction is scoped to history-only paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sanitizeChatHistoryContentBlock()` now treats Responses media blocks the same as existing image/audio redaction when `redactInlineMedia: true` is passed from history paths only. Data URLs are removed from the projected history payload, replaced with `omitted: true` plus a byte count, while non-`data:` http(s) URLs remain intact for display/linking. Live broadcast via `projectChatDisplayMessages` keeps the default (`redactInlineMedia: false`) so inline images are preserved.

All chat.history-style callers now opt in: main gateway (`chat.ts`), session SSE snapshots (`session-history-state.ts`), embedded gateway stub, and TUI embedded backend.

## User Impact

Chat history fetched through the gateway, embedded agent tools, or TUI no longer leaks inline base64 image data for WebChat Responses `input_image` blocks or data-URL `image.url` blocks. Operators and users still see that media was present (via `omitted` + `bytes`) without shipping the raw payload over the wire. Remote https image links continue to display normally. Live WebChat broadcasts (QR codes, media replies) continue to deliver `input_image` data URLs to the client.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```text
pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts -- -t "sanitizeChatHistoryMessages"
# 12 passed

pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts -- -t "broadcast|input_image|media"
# 90 passed

pnpm test src/agents/tools/embedded-gateway-stub.test.ts -- -t "chat.history"
# 11 passed

pnpm test src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts -- -t "embedded TUI history"
# 1 passed (redactInlineMedia asserted on loadHistory)
```

New/updated cases cover:
- sanitizer shapes: `input_image.image_url`, `image.url`, `image.source.data`, nested `image_url.url`, https preservation, broadcast preservation
- embedded gateway stub: all `chat.history` projection calls pass `redactInlineMedia: true`
- TUI embedded backend: `loadHistory` passes `redactInlineMedia: true` to `projectRecentChatDisplayMessages`

### Real behavior proof (outside Vitest)

```text
node --import tsx scripts/proof-chat-history-sanitize-input-image.mjs
# All proof checks passed (8 cases including projectRecentChatDisplayMessages history path)
```

target.title: feat(session): add includeArchived to chat.history and sessions_history
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the read-only path of [#45003](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45003)'s 3-PR roadmap: give agents and `chat.history` callers a way to recover context that lives in `.reset.<ts>` archives, **without** resurrecting those archives as live sessions.

This PR closes the three concrete upstream gaps identified by clawsweeper / Codex review on [issue #45003 (2026-04-28T22:20:54Z)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45003#issuecomment-4337189378):

> - sessions_history has no archive selector
> - chat.history reads current active transcript only
> - Protocol schema has no archived-history parameter

## Changes

### Protocol (additive, backwards-compatible)

- `src/gateway/protocol/schema/logs-chat.ts` — `ChatHistoryParamsSchema` gains an optional `includeArchived: boolean`. Default `false` preserves all current behavior.

### Gateway helpers

- `src/gateway/session-transcript-files.fs.ts` — new `listResetArchivesForSession(sessionId, searchDirs)` lists every `<sessionId>.jsonl.reset.<ts>` archive sorted oldest-first.
- `src/gateway/session-utils.fs.ts` — new `readSessionMessagesIncludingArchives(sessionId, storePath, sessionFile)` chains archive segments before the primary transcript with synthetic system messages tagged `__openclaw.kind: "session-reset"` so callers can render dividers. Archive segments are parsed line-by-line; the primary segment delegates to the existing `readSessionMessages` so it still gets `SessionManager` active-branch treatment for tree-format transcripts.

### Gateway handler

- `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` — `chat.history` reads `includeArchived` from params and dispatches to the new aggregator only when explicitly `true`.

### Agent tool

- `src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts` — `SessionsHistoryToolSchema` gains optional `includeArchived`. The tool forwards the flag verbatim to the `chat.history` call.

## Tests

- `src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts` — 6 new tests:
  - default behavior unchanged when no archives exist
  - archive content surfaced when primary missing
  - multiple archives chained chronologically before primary, each with a session-reset boundary marker
  - empty result when neither primary nor any archive exists
  - other sessions' archives are not pulled in
  - empty `sessionId` short-circuits
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.test.ts` — 2 new tests verifying the param is plumbed through from tool → `chat.history`.

## Design notes

This is the **read-only** path of the #45003 roadmap. It does not rename, move, or otherwise mutate archive files: archives stay archived, the user opts into visibility for one query at a time. That keeps it consistent with the existing "archive lifecycle is one-way" precedent (`sessions.delete` has no undo) and avoids the compaction-chain checkpoint and session-memory-hook double-summary risks that come with any unarchive/restore design.

`includeArchived` is also a user-explicit opt-in (not an automatic fallback), so it is consistent with `/reset` semantics: the user is asking for the recovery view, not having archived content silently re-injected into automated paths.

## Verification

- Scoped tests: `pnpm test src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts` — 60/60 pass (54 originals + 6 new).
- Type-check: `pnpm tsgo:core` introduces 0 new errors on the touched files (verified by stash-toggle baseline comparison).
- Manual: production gateway built from this branch and started on `:18789` against the local production data dir; `chat.history` RPC with `includeArchived: true` returns chained archive segments with `session-reset` boundary markers, while the default (`false` / omitted) returns the same set as before.

## Related work

- Fixes part of #45003 (PR 3 of the original 3-PR roadmap).
- Companion PRs in the same area, **all touching disjoint code paths**:
  - #60409 — `chat.history` fallback to most recent reset archive when primary is missing (PR 1 of the roadmap; in flight, CI green).
  - #71537 — `session-memory` hook + `session-logs` skill archive support (touches `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/*`, no overlap with this PR).
  - #68765 — compaction checkpoint chain reset semantics; explicitly defers non-chained reset-archive fallback to #60409.

﻿## Summary

- Fix `resolveModelAuthLabel` so `/status` and other UI surfaces show the same auth source as runtime resolution for custom providers like `zai-light`.

Closes #82020

## Real behavior proof

The fix makes `resolveModelAuthLabel` agree with `resolveApiKeyForProvider`: the `zai-light` per-entry literal key is reported as `api-key (models.json)`, and generic late custom-key fallback no longer masks env labels.

Real environment tested: Local Windows checkout (`D:\WorkSpace\AI\openclaw`) with Node `v24.13.1` and pnpm `11.2.2`, using the PR branch `fix/provider-auth-label-82020` after the patch.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```powershell
pnpm exec tsx -e "(async()=>{const { resolveModelAuthLabel } = await import('./src/agents/model-auth-label.ts'); const { resolveApiKeyForProvider } = await import('./src/agents/model-auth.ts'); const cfg={models:{providers:{zai:{api:'openai-completions',baseUrl:'https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/coding/paas/v4',apiKey:'zai-api-key',models:[]},'zai-light':{api:'openai-completions',baseUrl:'https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/coding/paas/v4',apiKey:'sk-light-only',models:[{id:'glm-5-turbo',name:'glm-5-turbo',reasoning:false,input:['text'],cost:{input:0,output:0,cacheRead:0,cacheWrite:0},contextWindow:8192,maxTokens:4096}]}}}}; process.env.ZAI_API_KEY='zai-env-key'; const auth=await resolveApiKeyForProvider({provider:'zai-light',cfg}); const label=resolveModelAuthLabel({provider:'zai-light',cfg}); console.log(JSON.stringify({authSource:auth.source,authKey:auth.apiKey,label},null,2));})();"
```

target.title: fix(skills): require resolved approval before mutating actions
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: several skill docs mention confirmation near mutating commands, but do not always bind approval to the resolved target/content.
- Solution: require preview or resolution first, then approval of the exact action before send/reorder/upload-style commands.
- What changed: tightened the instructions for `ordercli`, `imsg`, `gog`, `wacli`, and `oracle`.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no CLI code, command syntax, installer metadata, or changelog changes.

## Motivation

This came from a research pass over skill semantics around real side effects.

One concrete case is `ordercli`. Before this patch, the doc listed:

```bash
ordercli foodora reorder <orderCode> --confirm --address-id <id>
```

The missing guard was not the command itself; it was the approval object. A plausible flow is:

1. User says: "reorder my last sushi order, use the office address."
2. The agent resolves an order code and address ID.
3. The agent runs the `--confirm` command without first showing the resolved items, fees, substitutions, and address.

This patch makes the approval target explicit: preview or resolve first, show the concrete target/content, then run the mutating command only after that preview is approved.

The same pattern applies to messaging and mail. "Text Alex that I'm running late" should not send until `Alex` has been resolved to a specific phone/chat and the final body is shown back.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes N/A
- Related N/A
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: skill instructions now require a resolved preview before high-impact actions such as `ordercli ... --confirm`, `imsg send`, `gog gmail send` / calendar writes, `wacli send`, and Oracle uploads.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `skill-safety-gates`, commit `dd2c700ea0`, based on `origin/main`. I used the isolated dev profile so the proof did not depend on my normal `~/.openclaw` config.

target.title: [AI-assisted] Add session history family lookup
target.body:
## Problem

When a threaded conversation has already been split across reset transcripts, `chat.history` and the `sessions_history` tool only read the currently active transcript. The session store can already retain the family through `usageFamilySessionIds`, but history readers do not use that chain and do not discover archived `*.jsonl.reset.<timestamp>` topic transcripts.

That means an agent/tool can be looking at the correct logical Telegram/Slack/Discord thread and still miss earlier turns after session rollover.

## Fix

Add an opt-in family history path:

- `chat.history` accepts `includeFamily: true`.
- `sessions_history` accepts `includeFamily`.
- Gateway and embedded `chat.history` now share the bounded/header-checked reset archive resolver instead of using separate prefix scans.
- The shared resolver can include owned topic-suffixed reset archives such as `<sessionId>-topic-456.jsonl.reset.<timestamp>` only when the archive header matches the requested session id.
- Same-prefix colliding topic archives and headerless topic archives are ignored.
- Family read targets are capped before transcript reads, and normal `chat.history` behavior remains opt-in: UI startup does not load ancestor history.

target.title: fix(codex): honor tool result cap in app-server transcripts
target.body:
## Summary

Codex app-server transcript projection had its own hardcoded tool-output cap (`12_000` chars), so configured OpenClaw limits such as `agents.defaults.contextLimits.toolResultMaxChars = 8000` did not apply before tool output was mirrored into the native app-server thread.

This PR makes `CodexAppServerEventProjector` resolve the configured default/per-agent `toolResultMaxChars` and apply it to both streamed `outputDelta` aggregation and final snapshot tool-result transcript messages. The truncation notice includes the original size and configured limit, with guidance to rerun using narrower tool arguments.

Scope boundary: this does not change dynamic tool execution payloads, the live/display sanitizer, or read-tool behavior. It only bounds the text that gets projected into the Codex app-server/native transcript.

## Motivation / Problem

On a local OpenClaw/Quill WebChat setup, repeated large `bash`/tool results were entering the native app-server transcript at roughly 20K-25K JSON-wrapped characters even though the OpenClaw config set `toolResultMaxChars` to `8000`. Those oversized transcript entries caused avoidable context bloat and lag during WebChat turns.

The latest beta still contains the separate hardcoded path:

- `dist/run-attempt-BMcMyAoZ.js`
- `const TOOL_TRANSCRIPT_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS = 12e3`
- `appendToolOutputDeltaText(..., delta)` and `truncateToolTranscriptText(text)` both use that local cap

Related to #84659, but not the same bug: #84659 is about live/display/read output clipping, while this PR addresses the Codex app-server/native transcript projection path.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests only
- [ ] Chore / maintenance

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Web UI / frontend
- [ ] Memory / QMD
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Agents / routing
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Other:

## Linked Issues

Related #84659

- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression.
- [ ] This PR implements a requested feature.
- [ ] No issue exists yet; details are in the evidence section below.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** The Codex app-server/native transcript path now honors configured default/per-agent `contextLimits.toolResultMaxChars` instead of always using the projector's hardcoded 12K cap for mirrored tool output. The patch also keeps raw tool output from spoofing the truncation marker and bypassing the cap.

**Real environment tested:** Local macOS OpenClaw setup running OpenClaw `2026.5.19` with the same projector logic backported into the installed runtime. Configured `agents.defaults.contextLimits.toolResultMaxChars` was `8000`. Latest npm beta `2026.5.20-beta.1` was inspected for the pre-fix hardcoded cap.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran an isolated real OpenClaw agent turn through the Gateway/app-server path, forcing one large `bash` result, then inspected the stored mirrored session transcript:

```bash
openclaw agent --agent main --session-id codex-proof-tool-transcript-cap-20260520 --message 'Local proof for Codex app-server transcript cap. Run exactly this shell command once: node -e "process.stdout.write(\"A\".repeat(12050))". Do not read files. Do not write files. After the command, reply with one sentence saying the command was run.' --thinking minimal --json --timeout 300

node - <<'NODE'
const fs = require('fs');
const storePath = '/Users/han.kim/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json';
const key = 'agent:main:explicit:codex-proof-tool-transcript-cap-20260520';
const store = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(storePath, 'utf8'));
const file = store[key].sessionFile;
const rows = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').trim().split(/\n+/).map((line) => JSON.parse(line));
const toolRow = rows.find((row) => row.message?.role === 'toolResult');
const text = toolRow.message.content[0].content;
console.log('sessionFile', file);
console.log('toolResultTextChars', text.length);
console.log(text.match(/truncated: original [^)]*/)?.[0]);
NODE
```

**Evidence after fix:** Copied live terminal output from the local OpenClaw setup after the backport:

```text
$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.contextLimits
{
  "memoryGetMaxChars": 6000,
  "memoryGetDefaultLines": 40,
  "toolResultMaxChars": 8000
}

$ openclaw agent --agent main --session-id codex-proof-tool-transcript-cap-20260520 --message '...' --thinking minimal --json --timeout 300
{

  "summary": "completed",
  "result": {
    "payloads": [{ "text": "The command was run.", "mediaUrl": null }],

      }
    }

}

$ node inspect-codex-proof-session.js

rows 5

```


Upstream source validation after patch:

```text
event-projector.test.ts: 61 passed

```

**Observed result after fix:** A real OpenClaw agent turn produced 12,050 stdout characters from `bash`; the app-server/native mirrored session transcript stored a bounded tool result of 8,107 characters, which is the 8,000 configured cap plus the truncation notice. The stored transcript included `truncated: original 12050 chars, limit 8000`, confirming the configured cap was applied before the tool result was mirrored into session state.

**What was not tested:** I did not install and run a full OpenClaw build from this PR branch in a separate clean machine. The projector behavior is covered by targeted upstream tests and was locally backported to the installed OpenClaw runtime for live setup validation.

## Root Cause

`CodexAppServerEventProjector` maintained a separate hardcoded transcript cap instead of resolving the existing OpenClaw `contextLimits.toolResultMaxChars` configuration. The dynamic tool/runtime cap and the app-server/native transcript cap had drifted into two different policy paths.

## Regression Test Plan

Added targeted tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts`:

- streamed `outputDelta` aggregation honors `agents.defaults.contextLimits.toolResultMaxChars`
- final snapshot/aggregated tool-result transcript projection honors per-agent `contextLimits.toolResultMaxChars`
- oversized raw snapshot output containing the truncation marker is still capped
- truncation notice includes original size and configured limit

## User-visible Behavior

Long tool-output entries mirrored into the Codex app-server/native transcript will now be shorter when OpenClaw is configured with a lower `toolResultMaxChars`. The transcript includes an explicit truncation notice and suggests rerunning with narrower tool arguments when omitted output is needed.

## Architecture / Data Flow

Before:

```text
command output -> app-server projector hardcoded 12K cap -> JSON-wrapped oversized toolResult transcript message
```

After:

```text
command output -> configured default/per-agent toolResultMaxChars -> bounded transcript result with truncation notice
```

## Security / Privacy

- [ ] Handles secrets, tokens, credentials, or auth state
- [ ] Changes external network calls
- [ ] Changes file-system access scope
- [ ] Changes subprocess execution behavior
- [x] None of the above

Notes: This only changes transcript text truncation inside the existing app-server projection path.

## Backward Compatibility

- [ ] Requires migration

Notes: Existing behavior is preserved unless users have configured a lower or higher `contextLimits.toolResultMaxChars`, in which case the app-server transcript now follows that configuration.

## Risk / Rollback

Risk: users may see less tool-output text in the native transcript when their configured cap is lower than the previous hardcoded 12K cap.

Mitigation: truncation now includes the original size, the applied limit, and a clear instruction to rerun with narrower tool arguments for omitted output. Rollback is reverting this patch to restore the previous fixed 12K app-server transcript cap.

## What Problem This Solves

Android node invoke handlers use `parseJsonBooleanFlag` for flags such as `includeSystem`, `includeDisabled`, `includeNonLaunchable`, `includeAudio`, and presence beacon `ok`/`handled`. target.title: fix(gateway): defer hot-reload restart when dist/entry.js is missing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pushing commits into a live production git checkout triggers the gateway's hot-reload while `dist/` is mid-rebuild. The watcher (`requestRestart()` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`) immediately sends SIGTERM to the current healthy child process without checking whether the replacement build is valid for the new checkout state. The new child cannot start → crash-loop until systemd's start-limit is exhausted (37-min outage, P1, issue #99603).

## Changes

Three layers in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`:

### 1. isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs, resolveHead)

Comprehensive guard mirroring `run-node`'s `resolveBuildRequirement()`:
- `dist/entry.js` exists
- Build stamp (`dist/.buildstamp`) has valid `builtAt`
- Build stamp git HEAD matches current checkout HEAD
- Config files (`tsdown.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`) mtime not newer than stamp
- Runtime postbuild stamp (`dist/.runtime-postbuildstamp`) exists with `syncedAt >= builtAt`

### 2. Deferred restart polling (1s interval)

When build is not ready, polls every 1s. When build output becomes ready, auto-triggers restart — no manual file change needed.

### 3. Exit handler guard

After SIGTERM/143 child exit, verifies build readiness before restarting. Prevents self-reinforcing crash-loop.

## Evidence

### Real gateway:watch proof (current SHA 03954beb)

```
REAL gateway:watch PROOF — SHA: 03954beb32ea
Hostname: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
Node: v24.13.1

─── 1. isBuildReadyForRestart ───
  ✅ entry.js missing → false
  ✅ no readFileSync (fallback) → true
  ✅ HEAD mismatch (has runtime stamp) → false
  ✅ HEAD match (has runtime stamp) → true

─── 2. Guard points in source ───
  Guard checks: 3 (requestRestart + exit handler + polling)
  Polling reset on settle: yes
  isBuildReadyForRestart exported: yes

─── 3. Unit tests ───
  Test Files  1 passed (1), Tests  24 passed (24)

─── 4. Lint ───
  Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

### Unit tests (24/24 passed)


### Broader regression (91/91 passed)

```

      Tests  91 passed (91)
```

### CI status

All checks-node-compact-small-* pass. Lint + type-check clean.

## Review

- AI-assisted: Yes
- **Partial mitigation** — prevents crash-loop; issue #99603 should remain open for transactional restart (build-then-swap)
- Competing PRs #99610, #99972 target same root cause; maintainers should choose one canonical fix

target.title: fix(tui): keep skill approvals in the terminal

## What Problem This Solves

Workspace skill changes initiated from the TUI currently forward plugin approval requests to configured messaging channels. The initiating terminal stays blocked while Telegram receives a generic security-style approval message with little workspace-skill context.

Closes #100250.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Route pending plugin approvals into the TUI session that initiated the tool call.
- Present the plugin, tool, severity, requested action, and allowed decisions in a terminal modal.
- Support both Gateway-backed TUI sessions and embedded `tui --local` through a process-local approval broker.
- Bind Gateway approval review to the authenticated internal TUI device instead of widening approval visibility.
- Suppress messaging-channel fallback only for plugin approvals; configured exec-approval forwarding remains unchanged.
- Refresh pending approvals after event gaps/reconnects and keep nested overlay focus ownership deterministic.
- Sanitize terminal control, newline, and bidi text before rendering approval content.

## User Impact

TUI users can review and resolve workspace skill changes without switching to Telegram. Telegram no longer receives these terminal-local plugin approval requests. Denial, timeout, reconnect, and embedded-local behavior remain fail-closed.

target.title: Add reset family carryover summaries
target.body:
## Behavior or issue addressed

Depends on #90239.

When a session has been reset/rotated, the active transcript can be clean while the previous reset archive still contains the latest compaction summary. The next embedded-agent prompt therefore starts without the carryover context unless the model/tool explicitly asks for family history.

This change reuses the session-family transcript resolver from #90239 and injects the latest reset-archive compaction summary into embedded-agent prompt context before the LLM boundary, but only when the active context does not already contain a compaction summary.

## Fix

- Move the #90239 family/reset transcript target resolver into a shared gateway helper.
- Keep `chat.history(includeFamily)` on the shared resolver.
- Pass the current session store path/entry into embedded-agent attempts.
- Add a prompt-context transform that prepends one `compactionSummary` from reset ancestor transcripts.
- Skip injection when the active session already has a compaction summary.
- Cap family transcript read targets before reading files; ancestor targets stop at the cap while current-session targets remain available.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main` and preserved the newer transcript-reader seam plus same-session reset fallback.

## Real behavior proof

**Current head proven:** `ba74ecd54e52c2416ab8f7906491266b989f529c`.

**Behavior or issue addressed:** A reset/rotated logical session should read bounded reset-family history through the shared resolver, keep current reset archive plus current active transcript available inside the cap, preserve the newest eligible ancestors even when an older retained ancestor has many reset-topic archives, and inject exactly one reset-family compaction summary before the embedded-agent LLM boundary.
