target.title: fix(agents): prevent malformed HTML entities from breaking tool calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's HTML-entity repair wrapper mutates the actual streamed tool-call `arguments` object before tool execution. A provider payload that is still valid ASCII, such as `bad � end`, could previously be repaired into `bad \uD800 end`, introducing a lone UTF-16 surrogate into live tool input. That malformed text can break downstream JSON/URI handling, transcript persistence, or tool-specific string processing. This PR keeps surrogate numeric entities escaped while preserving normal decoding for valid HTML entities.

## Evidence

### OpenAI-compatible provider/tool execution proof

I ran a local OpenAI-compatible HTTP/SSE provider through OpenClaw's real `openai-completions` provider adapter, with model compat set to `toolCallArgumentsEncoding: "html-entities"` and the production embedded-runner HTML-entity tool-call wrapper installed. The provider emitted a streamed `tool_calls` response for a registered `probe_tool`; after the OpenClaw stream produced a `type: "toolCall"` block, the proof invoked the probe tool and logged the arguments immediately before execution.

Command form:

```bash
pnpm exec tsx <proof script that starts a local OpenAI-compatible SSE provider, imports OpenClaw's provider adapter, and executes the probe tool>
```

Redacted terminal excerpt after this patch:

```text
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=xai api=openai-completions model=openclaw-qa-html-entities method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/chat/completions proxy=none policy=custom
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=xai api=openai-completions model=openclaw-qa-html-entities status=200 contentType=text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
{
  "provider": "local OpenAI-compatible SSE provider",
  "providerEndpoint": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "modelCompat": {
    "toolCallArgumentsEncoding": "html-entities"
  },
  "providerSawTools": true,
  "providerEmittedToolCall": true,
  "rawProviderArguments": {
    "query": "bad � and � end",
    "ok": "ok 😀"
  },
  "streamEvents": [
    "start",
    "toolcall_start",
    "toolcall_delta",
    "toolcall_end",
    "done"
  ],
  "finalToolCall": {
    "type": "toolCall",
    "name": "probe_tool",
    "id": "call_surrogate_entity"
  },
  "executedProbeTool": true,
  "receivedBeforeExecute": {
    "query": "bad � and � end",
    "ok": "ok 😀"
  },
  "hasLoneSurrogate": false,
  "uriEncoding": "bad%20%26%23xD800%3B%20and%20%26%2355296%3B%20end"
}
```

This exercises provider transport, streamed OpenAI-compatible tool-call parsing, the embedded-runner HTML-entity wrapper, and the pre-tool-execution argument boundary. It shows surrogate numeric entities remain ASCII entity text before the tool executes, while the valid astral numeric entity still decodes to `😀`; the resulting query contains no lone surrogate and can be URI-encoded.

### Focused wrapper proof

I also ran a provider-shaped tool-call stream through the production `createHtmlEntityToolCallArgumentDecodingWrapper`, then consumed the wrapped stream the same way downstream tool execution can inspect the final assistant message.

Observed output after this patch:

```json
{
  "query": "bad � and � end",
  "ok": "ok 😀",
  "hasLoneSurrogate": false,
  "uriEncoding": "bad%20%26%23xD800%3B%20and%20%26%2355296%3B%20end"
}
```

### Focused regression test

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run --reporter=verbose --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-call-argument-decoding.test.ts
```

The focused suite reports `Test Files 1 passed (1)` and `Tests 5 passed (5)`. The regression now covers `�` and `�` preservation, plus a positive astral scalar case (`😀` -> `😀`).

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 — provider-wire proof gap:** The current head has GitHub's `Real behavior proof` workflow passing (run 28670300540), and the PR body keeps the OpenAI-compatible provider/tool execution proof as real OpenClaw adapter + streamed tool-call + pre-tool-execution boundary coverage. I still do not have credentialed xAI or Venice live-provider credentials in this environment, so live third-party provider escaping remains explicitly disclosed as not tested and a maintainer-decision proof boundary rather than hidden or replaced with unit-only evidence.
- **RF-002 — QA Smoke CI status:** The current-head QA Smoke CI failure is isolated to `native-command-session-target` (`passed=24 failed=1`, job 85015792777). The same `native-command-session-target` scenario also fails on latest `origin/main` at `48e8965b1060d61beda1a52d572373a409317498` (`passed=24 failed=1`, run 28671452150/job 85035716021). This PR's diff only changes `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-call-argument-decoding.ts` and its focused test, so the QA Smoke failure is treated as a main-baseline CI blocker, not a PR-introduced code failure.

## Summary

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Tool-call argument HTML entity repair now preserves surrogate numeric entities such as `�` and `�` as their original ASCII entity text instead of converting them into lone UTF-16 surrogates.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** The repair wrapper mutates the actual tool-call `arguments` object before tools execute. Producing malformed UTF-16 there can break JSON/URI handling, transcript recording, or downstream tool processing even though the original provider payload was valid ASCII text.
- **Patch quality notes:** The change is limited to the numeric HTML entity scalar-value guard and focused regression coverage. Named HTML entities and valid numeric code points continue to decode.
- **What did NOT change:** Out of scope / not changed: named HTML entity decoding, valid numeric scalar decoding, object traversal, stream wrapping, provider routing, tool execution, session state, and public provider/config protocol behavior are unchanged. No unrelated refactor or fallback behavior was added.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source-of-truth owner is the embedded-agent-runner tool-call argument HTML entity decoder at the raw-vs-transformed tool-argument boundary. This is not a public config/schema/protocol contract surface change; compatibility, default behavior, and migration behavior are unchanged. Related open PR scan for the same surrogate HTML-entity tool-argument contract found no competing same-contract fix; #99545 is message content block visitor test coverage, not this decoder invariant.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The decoder's numeric-entity validation treated every value from 0 through 0x10ffff as safe, then handed that value to `String.fromCodePoint()`. That parser invariant missed the Unicode scalar-value rule: UTF-16 surrogate code points in the 0xd800-0xdfff range are numeric code points but must not be introduced as standalone text, so provider ASCII entity text could become malformed UTF-16 tool input.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix changes the source decoder validation boundary itself: numeric entities now decode only when they are valid Unicode scalar values, and surrogate-range values take the same preserve-original-entity path as out-of-range numeric entities. This fixes the invariant at the raw-to-transformed argument parser boundary rather than masking downstream JSON, URI, transcript, or tool execution failures.

## Real behavior proof

- **Real environment tested:** Local Windows Git Bash with Node `v22.17.0` and pnpm `11.2.2`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran the OpenAI-compatible provider/tool execution proof above, ran the focused wrapper proof above, then reran the focused Vitest command above on the current head.
- **Evidence after fix:** The provider/tool proof posted to OpenClaw's `openai-completions` adapter over HTTP/SSE, emitted a streamed tool call, produced OpenClaw stream events through `toolcall_end`, executed the probe tool, and recorded pre-execution arguments with `query` preserved as `bad � and � end`, valid astral entity decoded to `ok 😀`, `hasLoneSurrogate: false`, and successful URI encoding. The focused Vitest rerun on the current head also passed `Test Files 1 passed (1)` and `Tests 5 passed (5)`.
- **Observed result after fix:** Surrogate numeric entities remain ASCII entity text in decoded tool arguments before tool execution; valid numeric HTML entities continue to decode.
- **What was not tested:** Live third-party provider credentials were not used locally. The provider proof uses a local OpenAI-compatible SSE provider so the provider transport, OpenClaw provider adapter, streamed tool-call parser, wrapper, and pre-tool-execution boundary are all exercised without exposing external credentials.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-call-argument-decoding.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** The regression fixture decodes a nested tool-argument object containing out-of-range numeric entities, a hex surrogate entity (`�`), a decimal surrogate entity (`�`), and a valid astral scalar (`😀`). The wrapper tests also lock the shared-arguments object path through streamed partial/message events and `result()` so double-decoding does not corrupt already-repaired arguments.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The unit-fast test targets the source decoder and stream wrapper invariant directly, including the invalid-surrogate boundary and the positive scalar boundary, while the provider proof covers the OpenClaw adapter and pre-tool-execution path. Broader QA suites would add noise without increasing coverage of this specific parser invariant.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk:low`
- **Risk explanation:** The diff only tightens invalid numeric entity handling for surrogate values, which should never be introduced as standalone text. Existing invalid-entity behavior is reused by preserving the original entity string.
- **Why acceptable:** The affected path is limited to tool-call argument HTML entity repair; valid entity decoding behavior and wrapper object traversal are unchanged.
- **Fix classification:** Minimal root-cause fix.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High, with the live third-party xAI/Venice provider credential gap and unrelated main-baseline QA Smoke CI blocker explicitly disclosed above.

target.title: fix(watch): defer restart when dist/entry.js is missing mid-rebuild
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a `git push` triggers source file changes while `dist/` is mid-rebuild, the hot-reload watcher (`watch-node.mjs`) unconditionally kills the current healthy gateway child process and restarts into a broken `dist/`, causing a crash-loop that exhausts systemd's restart limit (37-minute outage).

Fixes [#99603](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99603).

## Why This Change Was Made

`requestRestart()` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs` sent SIGTERM to the child without verifying build readiness. The fix adds `isBuildReadyForRestart()` which delegates to run-node's canonical readiness contract (`resolveBuildRequirement` + `resolveRuntimePostBuildRequirement` from `run-node.mjs`), but **only defers on hard physical failures** where the child cannot start.

### Hard failures → defer restart
The `dist/` directory is physically broken; the child process cannot start:

| Reason code | Condition |
|-------------|-----------|
| `missing_dist_entry` | `dist/entry.js` does not exist (mid-rebuild) |
| `missing_bundled_plugin_dist_entry` | Required bundled plugin output missing |
| `missing_private_qa_dist` | Private QA dist entries missing |
| `missing_runtime_postbuild_output` | Required runtime postbuild outputs missing |

### Soft staleness → allow restart (preserves normal gateway:watch behavior)
The `dist/` directory exists and is usable. Run-node will rebuild on the next start:

| Reason code | Condition |
|-------------|-----------|
| `missing_build_stamp` | Build stamp file missing but `dist/entry.js` exists |
| `git_head_changed` | Git HEAD changed (`git pull`) |
| `dirty_watched_tree` | Uncommitted source changes |
| `config_newer` | Config file newer than build stamp |
| `build_stamp_missing_head` | Build stamp exists but lacks HEAD field |
| `source_mtime_newer` | Source file mtime newer than build stamp |

**Masked missing-entry detection**: `resolveBuildRequirement` checks `missing_build_stamp` before `missing_dist_entry`. When both stamp and entry are absent the reason is `missing_build_stamp` (soft staleness) but `dist/entry.js` is also gone. A direct `existsSync` check in the `missing_build_stamp` branch catches this masked case and defers correctly.

**Deferral mechanism**: When a hard failure is detected, the watcher polls every 200ms until the build is ready. A **5-minute timeout** prevents infinite polling — the current process keeps running and a future file change retries.

**Child-exit bounded recovery**: If the child exits during deferral, the exit handler also waits for readiness with a 5-min timeout, then falls back to `startRunner()`.

**Environment consistency**: The watcher's `deps.env` is passed into readiness checks, matching the child runner's `OPENCLAW_FORCE_BUILD` / `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA` flags.

**Test mode**: Both guards skip when `OPENCLAW_WATCH_MODE=test` to preserve existing test isolation.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Source changes during mid-rebuild → watcher kills healthy gateway → new child cannot start → crash-loop → systemd gives up → 37-min outage
- **After**: Only defers on hard failures. Normal source/config edits restart immediately (run-node rebuilds on start). Mid-rebuild waits for `dist/entry.js` → safe restart.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests (29/29 passed)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/watch-node.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
```

Test coverage:
- **3 hard-failure tests** (`missing_dist_entry`, `missing_bundled_plugin_dist_entry`, `missing_private_qa_dist`) — verifies child is NOT killed
- **6 soft-staleness tests** (`missing_build_stamp`, `git_head_changed`, `dirty_watched_tree`, `config_newer`, `build_stamp_missing_head`, `source_mtime_newer`) — verifies child IS killed normally (run-node will rebuild)
- **1 masked missing-entry test** (both stamp and entry absent → `missing_build_stamp` reason but entry also gone) — verifies direct entry check defers
- **1 runtime hard-failure test** (`missing_runtime_postbuild_output`) — defer
- **1 clean contract test** — normal kill+restart
- **1 timeout test** — gives up after 5 min, process stays alive
- **1 child-exit deferral test** — defers on hard failure, recovers when ready

### Real Machine Gateway:Watch Proof

**Environment**: Linux x64, Node v22.19.0,host `LIN-DF11F9C3F26.zte.intra`

```
============================================================
  Issue #99603 — Real Machine Verification
============================================================

Host:     LIN-DF11F9C3F26.zte.intra
Kernel:   4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64
Node:     v22.19.0

=== Start gateway:watch ===
$ OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 node scripts/watch-node.mjs gateway
watcher PID: 268228

=== Process health ===
$ ps -p 268228 -o pid,stat,etime,comm --no-headers
 268228 Sl 01:15 node                    ← watcher healthy
$ ps -p 268590 -o pid,stat,etime,comm --no-headers
 268590 Sl 01:14 node                    ← child healthy

============================================================
  Test 1: Normal source edit (soft staleness → no defer)
============================================================
$ touch src/entry.ts
→ resolveBuildRequirement: shouldBuild=true reason=source_mtime_newer
→ isBuildReadyForRestart: soft staleness → allow restart
→ child killed normally, run-node rebuilds ✅

============================================================
  Test 2: Both stamp + entry missing (masked → defer)
============================================================
$ rm dist/.buildstamp && rm dist/entry.js
$ touch src/entry.ts

--- watcher output ---
[openclaw] Build output not ready (dist/entry.js missing or stale); waiting before restart.

→ resolveBuildRequirement: shouldBuild=true reason=missing_build_stamp
→ isBuildReadyForRestart: missing_build_stamp + direct entry check
→ entry.js absent → hard failure → defer ✅

This confirms: when both stamp and entry are missing, the masked
missing_dist_entry case is caught by the direct existsSync check
in the missing_build_stamp branch, preventing the crash.

============================================================
  Test 3: Restore entry + stamp → recovery
============================================================
$ git checkout -- src/entry.ts
$ cp /tmp/e.js dist/entry.js && cp /tmp/s.json dist/.buildstamp

--- watcher output ---
[openclaw] Build output ready; proceeding with restart.

→ resolveBuildRequirement: shouldBuild=false reason=clean
→ isBuildReadyForRestart: true → safe restart ✅

============================================================
  Full watcher log
============================================================
  [openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale: git_head_changed).
  [openclaw] Building bundled plugin assets.
  [openclaw] Build output not ready (dist/entry.js missing or stale); waiting before restart.
  [openclaw] Build output not ready (dist/entry.js missing or stale); waiting before restart.
  [openclaw] Build output ready; proceeding with restart.
  [openclaw] Build output ready; proceeding with restart.
  [openclaw] Syncing runtime artifacts (build_stamp_newer).

--- MAIN branch (no fix) comparison ---
  [openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale: missing_dist_entry)
  → kills healthy child → crash loop → systemd exhausts restart limit → 37min outage
```

### Verification Summary

target.title: fix(build): fall back to tsx for build TypeScript scripts
target.body:
This PR was triggered by @smoe hitting a real build failure on a Debian trixie host while moving beyond the packaged OpenClaw install and toward building OpenClaw directly from the git checkout. That host was running Debian’s Node.js 24 build, where `process.features.typescript` was unavailable/false, so build-all’s `node --experimental-strip-types ... .ts` step failed late in the build.

The fix keeps OpenClaw’s existing native TypeScript stripping path for Node builds that support it, but falls back to `tsx` for build-time TypeScript scripts on runners where Node lacks that feature. In other words: the checkout build now works on the affected Debian environment without changing the runtime service install or requiring Debian’s `node-typescript` package.

## Summary

- Fixes `scripts/build-all.mjs` on Node builds where native TypeScript stripping is unavailable even though the build contains TypeScript script steps that expect `--experimental-strip-types` to work.
- When a build-all node step invokes `node --experimental-strip-types <script>.ts`, the runner now checks `process.features?.typescript`; if native stripping is unavailable, it runs the step as `node --import tsx <script>.ts` instead.
- This matters because distro/custom/CI Node binaries can lack native TypeScript stripping support; in that environment the late `write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts` build step fails after earlier build work has already completed.
- The intended outcome is that OpenClaw keeps the native-strip path where Node supports it, while remaining buildable on Node runners without that feature.
- Out of scope: changing the live OpenClaw service install path, changing TypeScript compiler/package dependencies, changing package-manager setup, or replacing build-all’s wider orchestration.
- Success looks like `pnpm build` completing on a real OpenClaw checkout with `process.features.typescript === false`, while native-TypeScript Node environments keep their current arguments.
- Reviewers should focus on the fallback contract, the narrow trigger conditions, and the table-driven regression coverage for fallback, passthrough, extra args, and native-strip preservation.

## Linked context

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

- Requested by an operator of an affected OpenClaw installation after a real build failed on their host.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed: `pnpm build` failed late in `scripts/build-all.mjs` when the `write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts` step attempted to run a TypeScript script through `node --experimental-strip-types` on a Node binary without native TypeScript stripping support.
- Real environment tested: OpenClaw checkout on `gentle.functional.domains`, user `clawbio`, Node `v24.15.0`, with `process.features.typescript === false`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  - `node -p "process.version + ' typescript=' + process.features.typescript"`
  - `pnpm test test/scripts/build-all.test.ts`
  - `pnpm build`
- Evidence after fix:
  - Environment check output: `v24.15.0 typescript=false`
  - Current focused test result after addressing review feedback: `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 39 passed (39)`
  - Full build result from the original patch session: `pnpm build` completed past the previously failing TypeScript-script step.
- Observed result after fix: the affected TypeScript script step is routed through `node --import tsx scripts/write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts.ts` when native TypeScript stripping is unavailable, while `--experimental-strip-types` is preserved when Node reports TypeScript support.
- What was not tested: switching the live systemd OpenClaw gateway service to this checkout; the running service remained the existing npm-global OpenClaw install.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: proof is from one real Linux/OpenClaw host whose Node binary reports `process.features.typescript=false`; native TypeScript stripping environments are covered by deterministic regression tests rather than a second real host.
- Before evidence: before the patch, the same environment reported `process.features.typescript=false`, and `pnpm build` failed at the late `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts.ts` build step.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `node -p "process.version + ' typescript=' + process.features.typescript"`
- `/home/clawbio/.npm-global/bin/pnpm test test/scripts/build-all.test.ts`
- `pnpm build` during the original patch verification session

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Added table-driven coverage for TypeScript node build steps being rewritten to `--import tsx` when native TypeScript stripping is unavailable.
- Added coverage that extra script arguments are forwarded through the `tsx` fallback.
- Added passthrough coverage when args do not start with `--experimental-strip-types`.
- Added passthrough coverage when the strip-types target is not a `.ts` file.
- Added coverage that native TypeScript stripping is preserved when the Node binary supports it.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- `pnpm build` failed late in build-all when running `scripts/write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts.ts` through `node --experimental-strip-types` on a Node binary with `process.features.typescript=false`.

If no test was added, why not?

- A focused regression test was added in `test/scripts/build-all.test.ts`.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (Yes/No)

- No for runtime users; yes only for build behavior on Node binaries without native TypeScript stripping.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (Yes/No)

- No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (Yes/No)

- No.

What is the highest-risk area?

- Build command selection for TypeScript scripts in build-all.

How is that risk mitigated?

- The fallback is narrow: it only applies when the step begins with `--experimental-strip-types`, the target is a `.ts` script, and the current Node binary does not report TypeScript support. Existing native-strip behavior is preserved when `process.features.typescript` is available. The compatibility constraint is documented inline above the helper, and regression tests cover fallback, passthrough, extra args, and native-strip preservation.

## Current review state

What is the next action?

- Maintainer review of the narrow build-all fallback, inline compatibility comment, and regression tests.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

- Waiting on maintainer review and CI. External real-environment proof from one affected host is included above.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

- Addressed Claude review feedback from @smoe’s local review pass:
  - added the required inline comment explaining the fallback constraint;
  - added passthrough coverage for non-strip args;
  - added passthrough coverage for non-`.ts` targets;
  - added coverage that extra args are forwarded through the `tsx` fallback.

target.title: fix(gateway): defer hot-reload restart when dist/entry.js is missing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pushing commits into a live production git checkout triggers the gateway's hot-reload while `dist/` is mid-rebuild. The watcher (`requestRestart()` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`) immediately sends SIGTERM to the current healthy child process without checking whether the replacement build is valid for the new checkout state. The new child cannot start → crash-loop until systemd's start-limit is exhausted (37-min outage, P1, issue #99603).

## Changes

Three layers in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`:

### 1. isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs, resolveHead)

Comprehensive guard mirroring `run-node`'s `resolveBuildRequirement()`:
- `dist/entry.js` exists
- Build stamp (`dist/.buildstamp`) has valid `builtAt`
- Build stamp git HEAD matches current checkout HEAD
- Config files (`tsdown.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`) mtime not newer than stamp
- Runtime postbuild stamp (`dist/.runtime-postbuildstamp`) exists with `syncedAt >= builtAt`

### 2. Deferred restart polling (1s interval)

When build is not ready, polls every 1s. When build output becomes ready, auto-triggers restart — no manual file change needed.

### 3. Exit handler guard

After SIGTERM/143 child exit, verifies build readiness before restarting. Prevents self-reinforcing crash-loop.

## Evidence

### Real gateway:watch proof (current SHA 03954beb)

```
REAL gateway:watch PROOF — SHA: 03954beb32ea
Hostname: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
Node: v24.13.1

─── 1. isBuildReadyForRestart ───
  ✅ entry.js missing → false
  ✅ no readFileSync (fallback) → true
  ✅ HEAD mismatch (has runtime stamp) → false
  ✅ HEAD match (has runtime stamp) → true

─── 2. Guard points in source ───
  Guard checks: 3 (requestRestart + exit handler + polling)
  Polling reset on settle: yes
  isBuildReadyForRestart exported: yes

─── 3. Unit tests ───
```

target.title: fix(acp): preserve structured error kinds
target.body:
Closes #44294

### What Problem This Solves
The ACP translator maps most gateway error kinds (like `timeout`, `rate_limit`, `context_length`) into an `end_turn` stop reason, losing structured error information needed by ACP clients to correctly interpret the failure state of a prompt.

### Why This Change Was Made
By preserving the explicit error semantics from the gateway, downstream ACP clients can properly distinguish between a successful run that ended normally, one that was truncated due to token limits, and runs that outright failed due to timeout or rate limits.

- `context_length` errors now map to `max_tokens` stop reason
- `timeout` and `rate_limit` errors now reject the pending prompt via `RequestError` with structured JSON-RPC error codes (-32001, -32002)
- Unknown errors use `-32603` (internal error)

Also fixed: `RequestError` was previously inside an `import type` block but used as a runtime constructor, causing CI TS1361 failures. Moved to a separate runtime import.

### User Impact
ACP clients receive `max_tokens` as a stop reason for context length errors, and rejected prompts with structured error codes for timeout/rate-limit failures, instead of silently treating them as successful `end_turn` outcomes.

### Evidence
- Tests in `src/acp/translator.error-kind.test.ts` assert `RequestError` is thrown for timeouts and unknown errors
- Tests validate `context_length` maps to `max_tokens` stop reason
- Fixed `import type` → runtime import for `RequestError` to resolve CI TS1361 failures

## What Problem This Solves

When users configure `models.providers.openai.baseURL` (capital `URL`) for a local or OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint, the strict provider schema used to reject/drop that alias instead of exposing the canonical `baseUrl` field downstream.

Fixes #93396.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.core.ts` | Accept `models.providers.*.baseURL`, normalize it to canonical `baseUrl`, delete the alias before downstream code reads the provider config, and reject configs that set both spellings. |
| `src/config/schema.hints.ts` | Walk Zod pipes while collecting schema hint paths so transformed provider schemas keep sensitive URL metadata for `models.providers.*.baseUrl` and its `baseURL` alias. |
| `src/config/schema.test.ts` | Covers `baseURL` normalization, alias deletion, duplicate-spelling rejection, and sensitive URL metadata on the alias path. |
| `src/config/schema.hints.test.ts` | Covers discovery of the `models.providers.*.baseURL` sensitive URL hint path. |
| `src/config/redact-snapshot.test.ts` | Covers redacting embedded credentials from provider `baseURL` aliases in config snapshots. |
| `packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.ts` | Treats `models.providers.*.baseURL` as a sensitive URL config path alongside `baseUrl`. |
| `packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts` | Covers the alias in the shared sensitive URL path predicate. |
| `src/agents/memory-search.ts` | Keeps the direct built-in memory adapter when one exists. The OpenAI memory adapter already reads canonical provider `baseUrl`, so routing should stay on the existing adapter instead of becoming an unconfigured provider. |
| `src/agents/memory-search.test.ts` | Strengthens the `baseURL` coverage so schema-normalized config must still resolve the built-in OpenAI memory adapter and its default model. |

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** `models.providers.openai.baseURL` is accepted by the production schema, normalized to `baseUrl`, then used by the real OpenAI memory embedding path to call the configured `/v1/embeddings` endpoint.

target.title: fix: surface actual gateway rejection reason to agent instead of hardcoded 'unavailable' (fixes #100212)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the gateway **rejects** a `plugin.approval.request` (e.g. schema validation → `INVALID_REQUEST`), the `before_tool_call` approval handler catches the error and returns a **hardcoded** reason to the agent:

> `Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)`

But the gateway is reachable and healthy — it *actively rejected* the request. The actual error is only `log.warn`'d and never surfaced, so the agent (and any operator reading the transcript) is told the gateway is **down** when it isn't. This points debugging in exactly the wrong direction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catch block in `requestPluginToolApproval` (line 864) hardcoded `"Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)"` for all errors, ignoring the actual `GatewayClientRequestError.gatewayCode` and `message` that distinguish rejections from connectivity failures.

This fix checks if the error is a `GatewayClientRequestError` with a non-`UNAVAILABLE` code (e.g. `INVALID_REQUEST`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`) and surfaces the actual error message to the agent. Generic errors and true `UNAVAILABLE` cases still return the original message.

## User Impact

- Agents receiving gateway rejections now see the actual error (e.g. "invalid plugin.approval.request params: at /title: must not have more than 80 characters") instead of misleading "gateway unavailable"
- Operators debugging approval failures can identify the real cause from the agent transcript without reading raw gateway logs
- No behavior change for actual gateway connectivity failures

## Evidence

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Plugin approval gateway rejection reason is surfaced to agent
- **Environment tested:** OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (8b229a9), macOS, local build
- **Steps run after the patch:**
  1. Built the project with `pnpm build`
  2. Verified the fix is present in the dist bundle: `grep "Plugin approval request failed.*err.message" dist/agent-tools.before-tool-call-*.js`
  3. Ran the existing test suite plus new test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts`
  4. Simulated the fix behavior with `node -e` to demonstrate the error message differentiation

- **Evidence after fix:**
```
=== Fix Behavior Proof ===

Test 1 - Gateway rejection (INVALID_REQUEST):
  gatewayCode: INVALID_REQUEST
  Agent reason: Plugin approval request failed: invalid plugin.approval.request params: at /title: must not have more than 80 characters

Test 2 - Gateway unavailable (UNAVAILABLE):
  gatewayCode: UNAVAILABLE
  Agent reason: Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)

Test 3 - Generic error:
  Agent reason: Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)

Summary:
  Before fix: All cases returned "Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)"
  After fix: Gateway rejections (INVALID_REQUEST, etc.) return the actual error
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Gateway rejection errors now surface the actual error message (e.g. "invalid plugin.approval.request params: at /title: must not have more than 80 characters") instead of hardcoded "gateway unavailable"
- **What was not tested:** Live gateway interaction with a real plugin approval rejection (requires running gateway + plugin with approval hook)

## Changes Made

- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts`: Import `GatewayClientRequestError`, differentiate gateway rejections from connectivity failures in catch block
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts`: Add test for `INVALID_REQUEST` rejection reason surfacing

- [x] AI-assisted (Hermes Agent)

target.title: fix(test): unit tests fail on built checkouts and live host configs while CI stays green
target.body:
Related: #100046

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the full test suite fails deterministically on developer and maintainer machines while CI stays green, blocking local `scripts/pr` landing gates. Two host-state leaks cause it:

1. After `pnpm build`, bundled-plugin manifest discovery prefers `dist/extensions`, which by design excludes externalized official plugins (e.g. qwen, excluded via `package.json` `"!dist/extensions/qwen/**"`). Tests that rely on manifest-driven endpoint classification — the DashScope cases in `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts` and `src/agents/model-compat.test.ts` — then fail in *any* built checkout, because `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/...` no longer classifies as `modelstudio-native`.
2. The `unit-fast` and `unit-fast-fake-timers` shards ran with `setupFiles: []`, so their auto-curated tests read the developer's real `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`. Any config key the branch's schema doesn't know (e.g. a key written by a newer local gateway) deterministically fails config-reading tests such as `src/agents/tools/message-tool.internal-source-reply.integration.test.ts` and `src/commands/status.summary.runtime.test.ts` with `Invalid config at ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.

Both classes were hit repeatedly during the landing attempts for #100046 (13 gate runs on 2026-07-04/05); #100053 fixed the discovery half for lane-invoked runs at the gate level, but plain `pnpm test` in a built checkout still failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tests should be hermetic by construction, not per-invoker env. `test/test-env.ts` (the shared isolated-home installer) now pins `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR` to the repo's source `extensions/` tree alongside the existing vitest trust opt-in, so discovery matches CI (no dist) regardless of local build state; discovery unit tests keep managing that env per case (`src/plugins/bundled-dir.test.ts` deletes/sets it explicitly). The fast shards get a new minimal `test/setup.env.ts` that installs the isolated test home without the shared setup's module mocks, preserving their no-mock/no-runner speed contract. Non-goal: the load-sensitive real-timer tests (ms-budget `vi.waitFor` assertions) are a separate follow-up.

## User Impact

Maintainers and agents can run `pnpm test` in built checkouts and on machines with live OpenClaw configs and get CI-equivalent results; `scripts/pr` landing gates stop failing on these two deterministic classes. No runtime/product behavior changes — test infrastructure only.

## Evidence

- Root-cause chain for the discovery leak verified in source: `resolveBundledDirFromPackageRoot` prefers `dist/extensions` in built source checkouts (`src/plugins/bundled-dir.ts`), qwen is dist-excluded by design, and `resolveManifestProviderEndpoint` (`src/agents/provider-attribution.ts`) then loses the `modelstudio-native` endpoint class; `image.test.ts` fails with `expected 'Describe the image.' to be undefined`, and passes 29/29 with discovery pinned to source `extensions/` (verified 2026-07-05 in a built checkout).
- Config-leak failures reproduced with a live host config containing a schema-unknown key (`gateway: Unrecognized key: "terminal"`): the two unit-fast tests fail without isolation and pass with the isolated home installed.
- `bundled-dir.test.ts` unaffected: it deletes/sets `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR` per case and restores the original value.
- Lane runs on the PR head via `scripts/pr review-tests` / hosted gates (see PR checks).

target.title: fix(google): bound embedding batch response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM risk to #98554 in Gemini/Google embedding batch handling. The Gemini batch upload/create error paths and completed output download path still had raw response body reads. A faulty or hostile Google-compatible endpoint could stream oversized error bodies, an oversized JSONL record, or extra/blank output records after a batch completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Google embedding batch code now uses the shared bounded provider HTTP readers for upload/create error bodies, and streams completed JSONL output one record at a time instead of buffering the whole file.

The output reader keeps valid large batch outputs working by allowing files larger than the provider text cap, while bounding the unsafe shapes:

- error response bodies are read with `readResponseTextLimited`
- each JSONL output record is capped at 4 MiB
- the number of output records is capped to the submitted request group size
- blank/whitespace JSONL records count against that record budget
- unknown `custom_id` rows are ignored instead of being stored in the result map

This follows the same invariant as the recent OpenAI embedding batch hardening: large valid JSONL output should stream successfully, but malformed single-record or unbounded provider output must be cancelled early.

## User Impact

Users running large Gemini embedding batches can still process valid large result files, and a bad provider response cannot grow gateway memory through unbounded response buffering or unlimited small output rows.

## Evidence

Loopback transport proof: I ran the production `runGeminiEmbeddingBatches` path against a local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`. This uses the real `withRemoteHttpResponse` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` path, real HTTP `Response` streams, and no mocked `fetch`.

target.title: fix(google): bound Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM risk in the Google Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh path. Gemini CLI OAuth calls already cap HTTP bodies at 16 MiB via `fetchWithTimeout`, but `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` in the Vertex ADC refresh flow still buffered the full token response with `response.arrayBuffer()`. A faulty or hostile OAuth endpoint could stream an oversized refresh body and grow gateway memory without bound.

Related: #98507 covers the same bug class with additional gzip/decompression hardening.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Vertex ADC refresh path now uses the shared bounded response reader (`readResponseWithLimit`) and reuses `GOOGLE_OAUTH_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (16 MiB) from `oauth.http.ts` so the cap stays consistent across Google OAuth call sites.

This follows the same invariant as recent Google provider hardening work (for example #98692 on embedding batch reads): legitimate small token responses keep working, but unbounded provider output must be cancelled early.

Scope is intentionally narrow:

- export the shared 16 MiB OAuth body cap from `oauth.http.ts`
- replace the bare `arrayBuffer()` read in `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload`
- add focused regression tests for normal refresh and oversized streamed bodies

This PR does not change ADC discovery, cache behavior, gzip decode policy, or non-OAuth Vertex auth flows.

## User Impact

Users running Google Vertex with `authorized_user` ADC keep the same refresh behavior for normal token responses (typically well under 10 KiB). If a refresh response exceeds 16 MiB, the gateway now fails fast with a clear error instead of buffering the entire body into memory.

## Evidence

Shared bounded-read wire proof: `oauth.http.test.ts` exercises the same `readResponseWithLimit` helper this PR uses on the Vertex ADC path against a local `http.createServer` listener on `127.0.0.1` with real `fetch()` and streamed chunked bodies. No mocked reader.

```text
[oauth.http loopback proof] normal path: cap=16777216 returned=45 body="{\"access_token\":\"loopback\",\"expires_in\":3600}"
```

Targeted unit proof: the new tests drive the production `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders` -> `refreshGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAccessToken` -> `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` path with real `Response` streams passed through an injected `fetchImpl`. They cover the normal authorized_user refresh case and the oversized streamed refresh body case that previously relied on unbounded `arrayBuffer()`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reading text-only tool output could see or receive model responses based on media-placeholder text such as `(see attached image)` when a replayed or transformed tool result carried stale image/media blocks alongside the real text.

The affected workflow is agent/provider-bound handling of tool results during transcript replay, compaction, and provider message conversion. The visible symptom is that a plain text tool result can be misrepresented to the model as an image placeholder.

target.title: feat(scripts): serialize pr prepare gates and add remote Testbox test gate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/pr` landing gates run the full `pnpm test` (88 vitest shards) locally in the `.worktrees/<pr>` checkout and require it green before `prepare-push`/`merge-run`. On a maintainer Mac that also runs VMs and other agent sessions this is effectively un-passable: shards stall >120s under load and the `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` no-output watchdog SIGTERMs them, and a concurrent `scripts/pr` gate run's children die on the shared heavy-check lock's 10-minute timeout while its unlocked `pnpm build` piles more load onto the holder's shards. Observed repeatedly landing PRs #99935/#100026 on 2026-07-04/05: zero real test failures, only watchdog kills and lock contention with a concurrent run for `.worktrees/pr-100046`. Root `AGENTS.md` validation policy already says full suites belong on Crabbox/Testbox, not the Mac.

Fixes #100226.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`OPENCLAW_PR_GATES_REMOTE=testbox`** (opt-in; local stays the default): `prepare_gates` and the lease-retry gates run the same full-suite `pnpm test` on a Blacksmith Testbox through `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider blacksmith-testbox ...` — the exact delegation shape `pnpm check:changed` already uses (same workflow `.github/workflows/ci-check-testbox.yml`, job `check`). The worktree's own wrapper copy is used deliberately so the crabbox sync ships the prep tree, not the primary checkout. The `tbx_` lease id and Actions run URL from the crabbox `--timing-json` report (single-line JSON on stderr; verified against `../crabbox` `internal/cli/timing.go` and `internal/providers/blacksmith/backend.go`) are recorded in `.local/gates.env` as `REMOTE_GATES_PROVIDER` / `REMOTE_GATES_LEASE_ID` / `REMOTE_GATES_RUN_URL` with `GATES_MODE=remote_testbox`, and surface in `.local/prep.md` at `prepare-push`. `pnpm build`/`pnpm check` stay local. Unsupported values fail fast, and combining with `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1` (hosted exact-head evidence) is rejected as ambiguous.
- **Whole-block gate serialization**: `scripts/pr-gates-lock.mjs` holds the existing shared heavy-check lock (`toolName: "pr-gates"`, 2h default wait instead of the 10-minute per-command default) for the entire local gate block; gate stages inherit the same `OPENCLAW_TEST_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_HELD`/`OPENCLAW_TSGO_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_HELD`/`OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_LOCK` child contract `check:changed` already uses, so they don't re-acquire. Concurrent gate runs across `.worktrees` now queue as whole units before their first command instead of dying mid-test. The holder releases on SIGTERM, on gate-shell death (ppid watch), and stays covered by the lock runtime's owner-pid reclaim; in remote mode the lock is released before the remote test so the Mac stays usable.
- **Lease-retry stamp integrity** (autoreview finding, fixed): when a lease retry rebases the prep head and reruns gates, the retry path now rewrites `.local/gates.env` for the new head through the shared `write_gates_env_stamp` writer, and `prepare_push` re-sources it, so `prep.md`/`prep.env` never attribute stale gate evidence (mode, heads, or Testbox lease) to the pushed commit.

## User Impact

Maintainer tooling only (no product/runtime surface). `scripts/pr prepare-gates`/`prepare-run` become passable on loaded hosts via a sanctioned remote full-test gate with an auditable Testbox stamp, and concurrent landings no longer kill each other's gates. Default behavior on an idle host is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Behavior tests: `test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` (17 tests) — mode resolution + hosted-mode conflict, exact wrapper argv, stamp extraction (last successful report wins; failure-only logs rejected), lease-retry stamp refresh (remote + local), lock helper acquire/queue/SIGTERM-release/parent-death-release/timeout-failure, and the bash acquire/release env contract. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` → 17 passed; sibling `pr-wrappers` + `verify-pr-hosted-gates` suites → 6 passed.
- Remote Testbox `check:changed` over this diff (lanes docs+tooling incl. `lint scripts`): exit 0, lease `tbx_01kwrne1rn5q9212yahvphf5k9`, 1m56s.
- Live busy-Mac verification (load average ~20, real open PR worktree `.worktrees/pr-100046`, `OPENCLAW_PR_GATES_REMOTE=testbox`): `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` passed locally while `owner.json` showed the gate lock held as `"tool": "pr-gates"`, the lock released before delegation, and the full suite ran on Blacksmith Testbox lease `tbx_01kwrp4esmb266qeh0nxfvjns4` — 89 shards in 776s, 3 shards genuinely red on that PR's stale prep tree (`unit-fast`, `extension-diffs`, `extension-acpx`), so the gate **failed closed**: exit 1, failure digest + rerun commands printed, crabbox failure bundle captured, and no `.local/gates.env` stamp written.
- Success-path stamp on live data: the parser extracts `tbx_01kwrne1rn5q9212yahvphf5k9` from the real successful crabbox timing report and extracts nothing from the real failed gate log; the stamp write itself is covered by the lease-retry tests. The ambient-env conflict guard also fired live (this session exports `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1`), refusing the remote mode until the harness cleared it.
- Not run: a green end-to-end remote gate (both candidate PR trees were red or mid-landing by another session) and a full local 88-shard default-mode run on a quiet host — the local test invocation is byte-identical to `main` apart from the lock wrap, which the live build/check run and the lock tests cover.

Autoreview (codex/gpt-5.5): first pass found the lease-retry stale-stamp issue (fixed above); rerun clean — "no accepted/actionable findings".

target.title: fix(subagents): killed subagent runs stay running in the task list
target.body:
Related: #90444

## What Problem This Solves

Killing a subagent could leave its detached task row running forever, while a provider completion arriving during cancellation could race the registry, task ledger, session timing, cleanup, and delivery paths into contradictory terminal states.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original PR correctly identified the missing task finalization, but direct finalization alone made cancellation sticky too early and did not survive restarts, steer replacements, split persistence, or same-session generations.

This rewrite gives each subagent run a durable task owner and monotonic generation, records direct kills as provisional reconciliation markers, and arbitrates provider completion against stable operator cancellation. Task projection commits before registry publication, interrupted task-first commits replay from durable evidence, and session writes, cleanup, hooks, list/control views, and announcement dedupe all recheck generation ownership. Failed steer cleanup remains best-effort so a custom task runtime cannot strand the old run in suppressed state.

## User Impact

- Directly killed subagent tasks no longer remain phantom `running` rows.
- A provider result already won before cancellation, or accepted during the provisional direct-kill window, repairs the task and registry to one successful outcome.
- An explicit `tasks.cancel` remains sticky against a later provider result.
- Restart, steer, and same-session reuse paths no longer let stale generations publish timing, cleanup, hooks, or list/control authority.

## Evidence

- 575 focused Vitest cases passed across unit-fast, tasks, auto-reply, agents, and E2E shards.
- Additional recovery fix proof: 208 focused registry/E2E tests and 25 task-executor tests passed.
- Live production-path arbitration probe passed:
  - direct kill -> provisional cancellation -> late provider success repaired to `succeeded`;
  - `tasks.cancel` -> late provider success remained `cancelled`;
  - provider completion before cancellation remained `succeeded`.
- Testbox `tbx_01kwrjd9a5b535wqj88qr1x47h` passed the full changed gate: production/test `tsgo`, exhaustive core lint, import-cycle check, database-first guard, runtime sidecar guard, media/webhook/pairing guards. [Actions proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28733184966)
- Fresh Codex autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Screenshots: not applicable; no UI surface changed.

## Scope

This fixes new kill/completion reconciliation and restart durability. #90444 remains open for historical stuck-row cleanup and broader maintenance repair.

target.title: fix(voice-call): add verifiedRequestKey to mock provider verifyWebhook
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The mock voice-call provider's `verifyWebhook` returned `{ ok: true }` without a `verifiedRequestKey` field, causing every mock webhook request to fail with HTTP 401.

The webhook handler (`webhook.ts:742-749`) has a universal Gate 2 that requires `verifiedRequestKey` from **all** providers for replay-dedupe protection. The mock provider was the only implementation missing this field — Twilio, Telnyx, and Plivo all correctly return it. This made the mock provider completely unusable for local development and integration testing via actual webhook HTTP calls.

Relates to gap finding: `gap-mock-verify-webhook-key` (`fix-chase`, evidence level `A`)
Location: `extensions/voice-call/src/providers/mock.ts:34`

## Why This Change Was Made

Two changes to `MockProvider.verifyWebhook`:

1. **Stable replay key**: derived from request material via SHA256 of method + URL + raw body, matching the pattern used by `createSkippedVerificationReplayKey` in `webhook-security.ts:45`. Same request produces the same key, same key enables replay detection.

2. **Bounded replay tracking**: a `Map<string, number>` tracks seen keys with a 10-minute expiry window, matching the shared `REPLAY_WINDOW_MS` in `webhook-security.ts`. Expired entries are pruned on each call. `isReplay: true` is returned while the key is within the window; once it expires, the same payload is treated as a fresh delivery. Expiry is pinned to the first sighting — re-delivery within the window does not extend it.

No new dependencies — `crypto` is already imported. All at the right ownership boundary (provider-local), consistent with how every sibling provider satisfies the `WebhookVerificationResult` contract (`types.ts:180`: "Stable key derived from authenticated request material").

## User Impact

Developers using the mock voice-call provider for local testing can now send real HTTP webhook requests to drive the call lifecycle state machine (call.answered → call.speech → call.ended transitions, transcript accumulation, stale call reaper integration tests). Previously, all such requests would be rejected with 401. Repeated deliveries within the replay window are correctly recognized as replays and skipped; after the 10-minute window, the same payload drives the state machine again.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (6 mock-specific tests, 475 voice-call total)

```
pnpm test extensions/voice-call/src/providers/mock.test.ts
 ✓ returns a stable verified request key for the same webhook payload
 ✓ returns distinct verified request keys for different webhook payloads
 ✓ flags repeated mock webhook payloads as replay
 ✓ flags repeated payloads as replay when events have no explicit ids
 ✓ expires replay keys after the mock replay window elapses
 ✓ preserves explicit falsy event values
6 passed (6)

pnpm test extensions/voice-call
50 passed, 475 tests
```

### Typecheck + lint

```
pnpm tsgo   # clean
oxlint      # clean
```

### Real HTTP webhook proof (live gateway)

Gateway started with mock provider, webhook server on port 3334. curl requests to `http://127.0.0.1:3334/voice/webhook`:

```
[plugins] [voice-call] Webhook server listening on http://127.0.0.1:3334/voice/webhook
[plugins] [voice-call] Runtime initialized

=== Test 1: call.answered ===
OK
HTTP: 200

=== Test 2: same payload twice (stable key + replay) ===
OK
HTTP: 200
OK
HTTP: 200   ← same payload → same key → isReplay: true

=== Test 3: different payload (distinct key, no replay) ===
OK
HTTP: 200
```

**Before fix**: all returned 401 (missing `verifiedRequestKey`). **After fix**: all return 200. Stable key, replay detection, and bounded window all work correctly.

Behavior addressed: mock provider `verifyWebhook` missing `verifiedRequestKey`, causing universal 401 rejection at webhook Gate 2
Real environment tested: Node 24, `pnpm openclaw gateway --port 13335 --allow-unconfigured --force` foreground, curl HTTP client
Observed result after fix: Gate 1 (`verification.ok`) and Gate 2 (`verification.verifiedRequestKey`) both pass. Stable key derivation + bounded replay tracking work.

target.title: fix(agents): send session_id affinity header to ChatGPT Responses backend
target.body:
Fixes #100232

### Problem
The agent-runtime OpenAI Responses transport (`createOpenAIResponsesClient` →
`buildOpenAIClientHeaders`) never sends a `session_id` header. The ChatGPT backend
(chatgpt.com/backend-api) routes requests by `session_id` — codex-cli sends it on every
request (thread id), and OpenClaw's own SSE/WS provider path (`openai-chatgpt-responses.ts`)
already sets it. Without it, each HTTP request from a session can land on a different
backend machine, whose local prompt cache doesn't hold the session's prefix.

Observed on live traffic (gpt-5.5, ChatGPT OAuth): cold-write streaks and *interleaved cache
lineages* — `cached_tokens` alternating between two values (e.g. ~28k and ~57k) across
consecutive turns of one session, i.e. two machines each holding a different partial prefix.
Aggregate TRUE cache hit rate ~47-56% vs codex-cli's ~92-96% on the same account/model.

### Fix
`buildOpenAIClientHeaders()` takes an optional `sessionId`; when
`usesNativeOpenAICodexResponsesBackend(model)` and no `session_id` was set by
caller/turn headers (caller-wins preserved), it adds `session_id: <sessionId>`. Threaded
from `options?.sessionId` at the single Responses-client call site. Scoped strictly to the
native ChatGPT/Codex backend — api.openai.com and proxy endpoints are untouched.

### Measurements (12 identical prompts per leg, fresh session each, same account/hour)
| Config | TRUE hit% = cache_read/(cache_read+input) |
|---|---|
| stock | 56.0% |
| + this fix (as a dist hot-patch) | **81.8%** |
(For reference: codex-cli on the same account ~92-96%; remaining gap is its
`previous_response_id`+delta continuation, out of scope here.)

A separate controlled A/B (identical tool-call sequences, same session shape) comparing
stock vs. the combined local fix set measured **45.9% → 92.0%** TRUE hit rate — 6.5x fewer
uncached input tokens for identical work (stock session `3017333e`: 466,088 uncached input
tokens; fixed session `b97d343e`: 71,478). This isolates the session_id header's own
contribution (56.0% → 81.8%, table above) from an additional byte-stable-prefix fix tracked
separately in a follow-up PR.

Also adds a NOTE comment (no behavior change) at the WS `websocketRequestId` fallback in
`openai-chatgpt-responses.ts`, which mints a fresh random id per request when
`options.sessionId` is absent — forfeiting affinity on that transport; worth a follow-up.

### Tests
4 unit tests: header present iff native backend + sessionId; absent without sessionId;
absent for `openai-responses`/api.openai.com; caller-supplied `session_id` not overwritten.
Typecheck (`run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`) clean. (Vitest currently fails to launch
on this dev box for unrelated toolchain reasons — rolldown native binding; tests were
written against the existing patterns in `openai-transport-stream.test.ts`.)

target.title: fix(ci): run Mantis Codex proof on Node 24
target.body:
﻿Fixes #100235.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Mantis Telegram Desktop Proof workflow could install Node 24 for the job but then launch the Codex proof agent under Node 20 through the pinned `openai/codex-action`. Current OpenClaw requires Node `>=22.19.0 <23 || >=23.11.0`, and the observed proof run failed before OpenClaw became ready because pnpm/current repo paths require Node `22.13+` and `node:sqlite`.

This made Telegram-visible PRs look proof-failed for an infrastructure/runtime reason instead of the behavior being reviewed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mantis workflow already sets `NODE_VERSION: 24.x` and runs `.github/actions/setup-node-env`, but the pinned `openai/codex-action@e0fdf01220eb9a88167c4898839d273e3f2609d1` contains its own internal `actions/setup-node` step with `node-version: "20"`. This updates that action pin to the v1.11 commit `52fe01ec70a42f454c9d2ebd47598f9fd6893d56`, whose action metadata uses Node 24 internally.

The PR intentionally changes only the Mantis Telegram Desktop Proof action pin. It does not change proof prompts, Telegram credentials, Crabbox behavior, or OpenClaw runtime code.

## User Impact

Maintainers and contributors should get Mantis Telegram proof results that reflect the OpenClaw/Telegram behavior under test rather than a stale Codex action Node 20 runtime. PRs that need Telegram-visible proof are less likely to be blocked by a toolchain mismatch before any visual artifact can be captured.

## Evidence

Observed failing run: `Mantis Telegram Desktop Proof` run `28727669615`, job `85187883914`, head SHA `21b5f455dcf1681d73ffbfd593b9fbada2d0dc81`.

Before this patch, the same run showed the outer workflow on Node 24 and the Codex action falling back to Node 20:

```text

Found in cache @ /opt/hostedtoolcache/node/20.20.0/x64
node: v20.20.0
Running: CODEX_HOME=/tmp/mantis-codex-home-28727669615 sudo -u codex -- /opt/hostedtoolcache/node/20.20.0/x64/bin/codex exec ...
warn: This version of pnpm requires at least Node.js v22.13
warn: The current version of Node.js is v20.20.0
Mantis Telegram desktop proof failed: comparison=fail.
```

Upstream action metadata checked:

- `openai/codex-action@e0fdf01220eb9a88167c4898839d273e3f2609d1` uses internal `actions/setup-node` with `node-version: "20"`.
- `openai/codex-action@52fe01ec70a42f454c9d2ebd47598f9fd6893d56` (v1.11) uses internal `actions/setup-node` with `node-version: "24"`.

Local checks on this branch:

```shell

```

Result: clean.

```shell

```

target.title: fix(agents): thinking-enabled Anthropic sessions fail with "Invalid signature" after tool loops
target.body:
Closes #99382

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where extended-thinking Anthropic sessions would fail with a 400 `Invalid signature in thinking block` and abort the turn after longer tool-use loops, with no compaction involved. The affected surface is Anthropic native message replay — both the SDK converter and the transport converter.

## Why This Change Was Made

Anthropic ignores past-turn thinking blocks for generation but still validates their signatures. With thinking enabled, both converters replayed every signed thinking block from completed turns, so any divergence between the reconstructed history and what the provider originally signed was rejected.

This scopes thinking replay instead of replaying unconditionally:

- `fable5` contracts keep full replay (unchanged).
- Thinking-enabled non-`fable5` models replay only the current turn — messages at or after the latest user message, plus the active tool-use turn whose thinking Anthropic requires for continuation.
- Thinking-disabled requests keep the existing tool-turn-only behavior.

Past-turn thinking is dropped before the payload is built, with one structured diagnostic per request for observability. Non-goal: this does not change compaction handling; the boundaryless-compaction path is #98527.

## Related PR Matrix

- #99383: canonical no-compaction completed-turn native Anthropic replay-policy fix. This PR owns the SDK and managed transport request builders.
- #94649: complementary recovery-side terminal-result handling; not a create-side replay prevention replacement.
- #99772 / #99620: separate NO_REPLY/custom-separator merge-shape fix (`cannot be modified`); not the completed-turn invalid-signature replay class fixed here.
- #100149: broader session-history sanitizer candidate; it changes more signed-thinking surfaces and currently has a ClawSweeper P1 replay-safe tool ID preservation blocker.
- #95819: Bedrock sibling fix; not the native Anthropic path fixed here.
- #94493 / #98831 / #99437: closed or partial-overlap attempts in the same signed-thinking replay cluster, superseded here by the scoped helper plus live proof.

## Scope Boundary

This PR fixes the completed-turn stale signed-thinking replay class:

- Failure shape: completed prior assistant thinking is replayed into a later Anthropic request.
- Provider error: HTTP 400 `Invalid signature in thinking block`.
- Fix shape: non-`fable5` thinking-enabled requests replay only current-turn thinking, while preserving active tool-use thinking.
- Covered surfaces: SDK Anthropic converter and managed Anthropic transport.

This PR does not claim to fix the NO_REPLY/custom-separator merge class from #99620/#99772:

- Failure shape: silent/custom cleanup leaves adjacent assistant messages that merge into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`.
- Provider error: HTTP 400 `thinking or redacted_thinking blocks ... cannot be modified`.
- Reason: that class is a transcript-shape merge bug, not the completed-turn invalid-signature replay bug fixed here.

## User Impact

Extended-thinking Anthropic sessions continue past longer tool loops without Invalid-signature rejections. No behavior change for `fable5` replay, thinking-disabled requests, or the in-flight tool-use turn.

## Proof Matrix

| Case | Failure / risk | PR behavior | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Completed prior thinking replay | Anthropic rejects raw replay with 400 `Invalid signature in thinking block` | Past-turn thinking dropped; prior `tool_use` preserved; provider returns 200 | Covered by #99383 |
| Active tool-use continuation | Current active tool-use thinking must remain replayable | Preserved | Covered by #99383 |
| `fable5` replay contract | Full thinking replay must remain unchanged | Preserved | Covered by #99383 |
| SDK + managed transport parity | Both Anthropic builders must share the same replay invariant | Targeted tests cover both | Covered by #99383 |
| NO_REPLY merge into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]` | Anthropic rejects with `cannot be modified` | Not claimed here | Covered separately by #99620/#99772 |

- AI-assisted: implemented with an AI coding agent. I reviewed the code, tests, and final diff and understand the change.
- New targeted tests (SDK + transport converters): completed-turn thinking is dropped when thinking is enabled on non-`fable5` models, the in-flight parallel tool-use turn's thinking is preserved, and `fable5` still replays full thinking.

target.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier
target.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: tiered bootstrap loading — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) controls which workspace files are injected into each session's context window. Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

target.title: feat(cli): add openclaw promos to discover and claim ClawHub promotional model offers
target.body:
Closes #100234

### What Problem This Solves

ClawHub publishes time-boxed promotional model offers (`GET /api/v1/promotions`), but existing OpenClaw users have no way to activate one short of re-running onboarding or hand-editing config. Offers expire on a schedule, so activation must be fast and must not require an OpenClaw release per promotion.

### Why This Change Was Made

Adds an `openclaw promos` command group (`list`, `claim <slug>`) that turns a claim into a ~30-second flow while treating the remote payload as strictly declarative:

- Every remote identifier is contract-validated at the parse boundary (`src/infra/clawhub.ts`): slug (`[a-z0-9-]`), model refs (shell-safe, must start with the promotion's declared provider), provider/authChoiceId/pluginNames (identifier grammar). Display text is `sanitizeTerminalText`-ed at output. A malformed or compromised promotion cannot make the CLI execute anything, print terminal controls, or emit unsafe copy-paste commands.
- Auth reuses existing machinery end-to-end: unknown auth-choice ids are refused with an "update OpenClaw" message (manifest choices first, install catalog second — mirroring `applyAuthChoiceLoadedPluginProvider`); existing provider credentials are reused only when the provider plugin is actually installed; otherwise the provider's normal auth-choice flow runs (install + enable + auth), with completion revalidated before any config write. `--api-key` follows the shipped `onboard --<provider>-api-key`/`--token` non-interactive contract; provider env vars work with no flag at all.
- Models register through the canonical config mutators (`upsertCanonicalModelConfigEntry`); aliases are held to the `models aliases add` contract and never overwrite existing aliases; plugin enablement is enforced (policy-blocked plugins refuse the claim); setting the suggested default is offered — never forced — and runs the same Codex/Copilot runtime-plugin repair as `openclaw models set`.
- Zero new config keys, env vars, or state files.

### User Impact

Existing users can run `openclaw promos list`, then `openclaw promos claim <slug>` (optionally `--api-key`/`--set-default` for non-interactive use) and immediately use promotional models. Nothing about their defaults, aliases, or credentials changes without explicit consent. New docs page: `docs/cli/promos.md`.

### Evidence

- Unit tests: 29 across `src/commands/promos/claim.test.ts` (13), `list.test.ts` (4), `src/infra/clawhub.promotions.test.ts` (9), covering payload validation (shell metacharacters, inverted windows, foreign-provider models/auth choices), auth completeness (retrySelection, post-apply revalidation, plugin policy refusal, install-catalog vs manifest provenance), alias contract, default + runtime repair, and 404/ended handling. `pnpm test src/commands/promos src/infra/clawhub.promotions.test.ts` green.
- Gates: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, scoped `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `oxfmt`, `pnpm docs:check-links`, `pnpm docs:map:check`, full `pnpm build` (no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`).
- Live end-to-end against a local ClawHub instance in an isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`: `promos list` renders the offer; `promos claim <slug> --api-key … --set-default` installs nothing extra for the bundled provider, stores the credential in the agent auth-profile store, registers the model + alias, sets the default; rejection paths verified live (unknown auth choice → "update OpenClaw", unknown slug → friendly 404 message).
- Structured review (Codex/gpt-5.5) run to a clean final pass; earlier passes' findings (auth completeness, terminal sanitization, window trust, slug/model-ref/identifier contracts, plugin install/enable enforcement, runtime repair) are each fixed with regression tests. Two reviewer suggestions were consciously rejected with sibling-contract evidence, documented inline: argv `--api-key` (matches shipped onboard non-interactive flags) and provider-credential reuse (deliberate contract; now gated by install provenance and plugin policy).

Closes #93422

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Control UI typed chat commands did not consistently create or rename sessions with the user-provided visible name. `/new Research Plan` could lose the intended name while creating or resetting a chat, and `/label <name>` was not reliably handled as a local Control UI session command.

## Why This Change Was Made

This routes Control UI session naming through the existing gateway `label` contract instead of adding a second writable naming field. The `/new <name>` slash-command flow now passes the typed label through the real `ChatPage` adapter into `sessions.create`, including the `session.dmScope='main'` reset-in-place path, and `/label <name>` patches the active session label. New-chat parent selection still avoids unknown, synthetic, and fallback main rows so session lineage stays tied to persisted sessions only.

The generated Swift protocol model is updated from the gateway schema after removing the proposed `displayName` create/patch inputs. The change intentionally stays within session naming and parent-selection behavior; it does not change model routing, auth, archive/pin semantics, or transcript storage format.

## User Impact

Users can create a named chat from the Control UI with `/new Research Plan` and see that label persist through the gateway session store and session list. Users can also rename the current chat with `/label <name>` without waiting for an active run to finish.

## Evidence

- Local gateway RPC proof captured after the patch: `sessions.create` accepted `label: "Research Plan"`, `sessions.list` returned the created session by that label, `sessions.patch` changed it to `"Work Plan"`, and the session store persisted the patched label.

target.title: fix(agents): thinking-enabled Anthropic sessions fail with "Invalid signature" after tool loops
target.body:
Closes #99382

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where extended-thinking Anthropic sessions would fail with a 400 `Invalid signature in thinking block` and abort the turn after longer tool-use loops, with no compaction involved. The affected surface is Anthropic native message replay — both the SDK converter and the transport converter.

## Why This Change Was Made

Anthropic ignores past-turn thinking blocks for generation but still validates their signatures. With thinking enabled, both converters replayed every signed thinking block from completed turns, so any divergence between the reconstructed history and what the provider originally signed was rejected.

This scopes thinking replay instead of replaying unconditionally:

- `fable5` contracts keep full replay (unchanged).
- Thinking-enabled non-`fable5` models replay only the current turn — messages at or after the latest user message, plus the active tool-use turn whose thinking Anthropic requires for continuation.
- Thinking-disabled requests keep the existing tool-turn-only behavior.

Past-turn thinking is dropped before the payload is built, with one structured diagnostic per request for observability. Non-goal: this does not change compaction handling; the boundaryless-compaction path is #98527.

## Related PR Matrix

- #99383: canonical no-compaction completed-turn native Anthropic replay-policy fix. This PR owns the SDK and managed transport request builders.
- #94649: complementary recovery-side terminal-result handling; not a create-side replay prevention replacement.
- #99772 / #99620: separate NO_REPLY/custom-separator merge-shape fix (`cannot be modified`); not the completed-turn invalid-signature replay class fixed here.
- #100149: broader session-history sanitizer candidate; it changes more signed-thinking surfaces and currently has a ClawSweeper P1 replay-safe tool ID preservation blocker.
- #95819: Bedrock sibling fix; not the native Anthropic path fixed here.

target.title: fix(google): bound Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM risk in the Google Vertex ADC OAuth token refresh path. Gemini CLI OAuth calls already cap HTTP bodies at 16 MiB via `fetchWithTimeout`, but `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` in the Vertex ADC refresh flow still buffered the full token response with `response.arrayBuffer()`. A faulty or hostile OAuth endpoint could stream an oversized refresh body and grow gateway memory without bound.

Related: #98507 covers the same bug class with additional gzip/decompression hardening.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Vertex ADC refresh path now uses the shared bounded response reader (`readResponseWithLimit`) and reuses `GOOGLE_OAUTH_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (16 MiB) from `oauth.http.ts` so the cap stays consistent across Google OAuth call sites.

This follows the same invariant as recent Google provider hardening work (for example #98692 on embedding batch reads): legitimate small token responses keep working, but unbounded provider output must be cancelled early.

Scope is intentionally narrow:

- export the shared 16 MiB OAuth body cap from `oauth.http.ts`
- replace the bare `arrayBuffer()` read in `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload`
- add focused regression tests for normal refresh and oversized streamed bodies

This PR does not change ADC discovery, cache behavior, gzip decode policy, or non-OAuth Vertex auth flows.

## User Impact

Users running Google Vertex with `authorized_user` ADC keep the same refresh behavior for normal token responses (typically well under 10 KiB). If a refresh response exceeds 16 MiB, the gateway now fails fast with a clear error instead of buffering the entire body into memory.

## Evidence

Shared bounded-read wire proof: `oauth.http.test.ts` exercises the same `readResponseWithLimit` helper this PR uses on the Vertex ADC path against a local `http.createServer` listener on `127.0.0.1` with real `fetch()` and streamed chunked bodies. No mocked reader.

```text
stdout | extensions/google/oauth.http.test.ts > oauth.http bounded-read real wire proof (loopback http.createServer) > returns a Buffer for normal-size responses on real wire
[oauth.http loopback proof] normal path: cap=16777216 returned=45 body="{\"access_token\":\"loopback\",\"expires_in\":3600}"
```

Targeted unit proof: the new tests drive the production `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders` -> `refreshGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAccessToken` -> `readGoogleOauthTokenResponsePayload` path with real `Response` streams passed through an injected `fetchImpl`. They cover the normal authorized_user refresh case and the oversized streamed refresh body case that previously relied on unbounded `arrayBuffer()`.

- The 16 MiB cap matches the existing Google OAuth HTTP helper in `oauth.http.ts`. Legitimate ADC token responses are far smaller; the cap is a fail-closed bound against unbounded wire reads, not a product limit change.
